Papo & Yo at heart is a puzzle game with platform elements.  The gameplay is based on testing things to see what they do and then figuring it all out.
The story is very rich and unique, as it unfolds you can see that it is surreal and metaphoric.
The pacing of the game is very good and the conclusion pieces the story together very well.
This is one of those games where the first playthough will be most of the enjoyment and you should consider avoiding looking up any spoilers.   Unlockables aren't available till the second playthrough in any case.
Overall if you like puzzles with a bit of platform style jumping thrown in and you like surreal metaphoric stories this is a good buy.

While the title on Steam just refers to this as "LISA", its full name is "LISA: The Painful", and this game can certainly live up to that name at times.
This game really feels like a side-scrolling version of Earthbound in an odd, post-apocalyptic setting, packaged into a not-so-kid-friendly game.
Before I actually start talking about what this game is like, let me just warn you: this game may likely destroy your emotions.
The story is hard to discuss without being spoiled, but this game has a very serious feel to it in certain moments. However, there are many exceptions. I've never seen a game pull off such a perfect blend of seriousness and comedy. One second, you'll be laughing/chuckling over something which just happened, and the next second, the game will suddenly switch into "serious mode"; the transition just feels so natural.
As for the gameplay, this is best described as a side-scrolling RPG game. If you liked Earthbound, you will most likely like this game as well. It even has music from Earthbound in it. Speaking of which, the game's soundtrack is also pretty great and always fits with the setting. There are moments you will absolutely hate the game, though.
Before you decide to turn down the game from that statement, hear me out. I know that makes the game sound terrible, but it purposely makes you hate it by forcing you to make decisions you don't want to make. Once again, I don't want to spoil anything, but personally, one of the decisions I made actually made me stop playing long enough for me to lose interest in the game, then eventually pick it back up again and complete it while having no regrets (other than the decisions I made). In other words, without spoiling anything, you will more than likely regret any decisions you make. There isn't really much of a "wrong" decision to make, but some are more beneficial than others.
This game certainly isn't for the weak-hearted or the innocent, but it's an amazing masterpiece with pretty neat (and sometimes grotesque) pixel graphics with a great story.
There's also a DLC expansion to this game called LISA: The Joyful, which is basically a sequel. However, despite the name, it's much less joyful than the original game. It's still a good DLC (which describes the story even further), but it doesn't have as many comedic feels to it as the original and is 100% serious at nearly all times.

I used to only play AAA games, wondering why anyone would want to play a game like LISA in the 21st century. But a friend convinced me to try it, and it become one of my favourite games. While some big productions will fade away from my memory with time, I'll never forget LISA. 10/10

, the reason why Sonic failed so bad in recent years, is not trivial things like Sonic's green eyes, homing attacks and Dr. Robotnik now being Dr. Eggman, the problems are SEGA and Sonic Team's incompetence, while Sonic 4 was made to be exactly what everyone wanted and still divided opinions, Sonic Generations has a lot of things that purist fans didn't want but still was liked by most people.

I give this a Yes, but with a very prominant question mark. I know I used to rip on other people for saying they didn't like a Biohazard / Resident Evil game just because 'it's not like the older ones', but this time, I can genuinely say that I felt alienated becaue it's nothing like the older ones. More specifically, it feels like this is just Capcom's answer to Konami cancelling Silent Hills. Honestly, it just doesn't feel like a Biohazard / Resident Evil game. It legitimately feels like Capcop presents Silent Hills. The only reason I recommend it is because it's a demo that looks and plays very well- albeit haveing awkward controls that I didn't see a way to change- and otherwise, I have to recommend playing it yourself just because A) it's free, and B) watching Let's Plays of it can't possibly convey the feeling of helplessness and isolation that you feel when you play it yourself. I've seen at least a dozen other people play it before, even seeing how to get the best possible ending. But when I was put in control, I just froze and forgot everything I'd studied.
TL;DR
Download it while you can because it's free, and will let you form an early opinion that no amount of YouTube footage can give you.

Rocket League is a great game in general. Nice developers that constantly update the game and are able to do that with non-mandatory DLC for extra cars. Had a fun time playing with friends; you probably will too.

The on think that has made me hate this game as of right now is intentonal throwing, three times in a row i ahd teammates who intentioanlly lost the game. One time a party of two veteran players threw the game despite how I asked to at least defend the goal they nevere responded. There is no option to report people for throwing games other than reporting them for unsportsman like conduct, and I feel my report won't be acted upon.

I rate games on a 1-5 scale ala X-PLAY (no decimals)
Rocket League is very straightforward and surprisingly fun for what little content it actually offers. There are multiple game modes but in short it is only online multiplayer soccer. Still the music partnership with MonsterCat is cool, The game rewards you with plenty of items to customize your car if you do not want to spend money. The cars really offer no advantages over each other either so there is no BS pay to win here. Sadly as with any game that is multiplayer driven it lacks much depth and get's old after awhile. Now that the game is 2 years old it is tougher to pick up the game as a new player and actually perform well. But for the price it is worth the money at least now. If the amount of players continue to drop this should see a price drop hopefully.
All in all, it's fun and addicting and should hold your attention for a good while.

Final Fantasy IX.
This will be an honest review, so if you're looking for a participant in the usual FF IX love fest...you might want to look elsewhere.
Played it when it came out. Finished it, never really gave it another glance. It lacked the panache of 4, 6, 7 and 8. It was just...a confluence of poor design choices being taped together like a bad collage.
It's not the worst Final Fantasy out there. That would be FF X-2. (Or, as I like to call it... Final Fantasy: The Hot Topic RPG).
But IX probably gets a lot of unwarranted love. It's a game pretending to be a JRPG without all of the more complex elements that made Square's previous RPG's so much deeper and intracate.
Final Fantasy IX is literally the most Americanized form of the Square RPG. As it was partially developed in Hawaii, with Americans...this is not at all surprising. The mechanics are dumbed down, the story is...fun, but drags you along. There are a lot of folks who love IX. That's cool. But it's not the best title in this franchise. Not the worst, but it approaches being truly terrible at times. If you have the resolve to push through...
The game would have been better, had IX not had so many plot holes. It would have been even a little better, if characters had more reasons for why they were doing what they were doing, and more defined....But more than that, for some of the most lovable characters, and for most of the set up they do....there's no payoff in the end. I won't spoil the story, only to say that...when you make your audience care about a character or characters......and then compare that character to a bunch of similar characters...and then don't resolve even 25% of that in the end....you fail at writing. FF IX is full of examples of really terrible character presentation and follow through. Way too many to list.
A lot of the story involves running to and fro for really trivial reasons. It gets to be a drag. There are highlights, like Eiko...but also characters who are shoe horned in...such as Amarant. He's really pointless filler.
It gets some things right too. Tetra Master is a much better card game than say, Triple Triad. The character design is really nicely done. It's just too bad they didn't make the best use of them. The antagonist of the game is only surface interesting. He's bad mostly for the sake of it. He offers none of the more dynamic and interesting behavior or motives of say...Sephiroth, Kefka, or even Ultimecia.
I bought the game simply for the sake of keeping my golden age FF collection going. I wanted to give it another chance, having played it years ago. While it is a visually stunning game at times...it's story is lacking, it's mechanics are really dumbed down, and It just feels like I am playing something held together at times by scotch tape and string.
I am giving it a thumbs up....if you like Final Fantasy games...it's a good buy. Good for a playthrough every 10 years or so. It's not a bad title...but the team who made it made plenty of choices that kept it from being great. If I could give it stars...it would get a 2.5 or 3 star rating.

This is the type of game that happens when you mix Earthbound and Undertale with The Walking Dead, Fallout, Wasteland, Life is Strange, The Last of Us, Max Payne, and Dark Souls. You get an RPG with toilet humor and emotional heartbreaking RPG tale that deals with a very heavy theme. It is one of those games that will break you in terms of both emotions and difficulty. It is also one of those games that will stay with you forever. Next to To the Moon LISA is one of the best RPG maker made games I have ever played. Can't wait to see what the developers of this game will make next.

Lisa is the ultimate RPG and a brutal game.  You will face incredibly difficult choices (such as losing limbs or party members) in a world gone mad.  There are laughs, gallows humor, and a bleak sadness that surrounds each chapter.  You truly feel like you are in the hopeless space that only a broken man's world can provide.
The first game to bring me to tears, Lisa is the toughest, funniest and saddest tale you could make out of a world full of perverts, buff dudes, traps and druggies.

Gameplay : 4/5
Sound and Music : 5/5

The gameplay is great and has a lot going for it but a lot of fights can be exploited once you learn how the system works well enough. The sound and music design is awesome and doesn’t stick to just one theme which lends to a lot of the scenes in the game. Visuals look really good but a good amount of assets get reused which makes some of the bigger fights not as impactful. I’ve played this game twice now just because of all the choices you can make throughout it which really help the game’s replayability. LISA is one of my favorite games and if anyone is looking for a game with a great story, this is it.

TL: DR; The best 3D Sonic Game since Sonic Adventure 1/2
Over the years the sonic team has launched many dissapointments for one reason or another.  Glitchy, horribly designed games that just never held up to the original series.  This game, however, is an incredibly successful take on the series.  Each level, taken from previous levels from the game franchise, is split into a 2d and 3d level.  These levels end up working incredibly well: they flow nicely, are unique to each game franchise, and are well designed.  Also many glitches which were in the previous games are nearly non-existant, allowing players to enjoy the game and levels as they were meant to be played.
There are some glitches in the game but they aren't nearly as prevelant as they are in other games, and many are great for speedrunning instead of breaking the game and causing the game to be unplayable.  Controller support is decent and now the game is old enough to run well on most setups without problems.
Lastly, the modding community really ran and expanded this game.  There are many player made levels out there that really increase the value of the game.  I have to admit I haven't explore this as of writing this review, but from what I can tell a lot of people have expanded gameplay value and are really increasing the longevity of the game.
Verdict: Buy it on sale, it's definitely worth it!

2K Czech's second take on the mob genre is a solid game through and through. While it is nothing even casual gamers have not seen beforehand, the gameplay is solid -- there is a mixture of driving, shooting, and good ol'-fashioned fisticuffs, as is the norm for games of this motif. The controls are good. The fighting portion of the gameplay is a bit hit and miss (no pun intended) -- it's simplistic and doesn't flow too well, but you won't find yourself in these situations too often throughout the game's storyline.
Speaking of which, this is undoubtedly the game's strong suit. You experience the story through the eyes of Vito Scaletta, an immigrant from Italy who comes to Empire Bay in the United States in the early 1900s in the hopes of finding a better life. There, he meets troublemaker Joe Barbaro who leads Vito through a life of crime. The game's general message is that all that glitters is not gold. As another reviewer mentioned, the game is not unlike watching a movie at times, which certainly isn't a bad thing.
Graphically, the game is quite impressive for its time, especially in comparison to the console ports. Some close-ups in the cutscenes haven't aged terribly well, but are adequate for conveying emotion.
Sound. The voice acting is convincing, and the game's rather liberal use of profanity leaves little to the imagination. The game is presented in surround sound, and there is plenty of directionality to transport the player into the game's immersive settings.
All in all, you're looking at a solid title with decent graphics, an immersive storyline with memorable characters, and good gameplay. Those interested in the mafioso genre should definitely check this one out, and those who don't should do so anyway.
AH! I almost forgot. Hidden within the game's missions are a variety of collectibles, of which a particular type will keep you glued to the screen for hours. Just...remember to clean your keyboard and monitor afterwards.

The world is mostly dominated by puzzles and platform jumping elements. Neither of them are particularly challenging.
Only when Monster decides to stop being a saggy sleepyhead, then things can get a little intense.
Ars Technica explains the plot brilliantly: "The game does an admirable job of telling its story through its environments and dreamlike situations, rather than belaboring the point with overly explanatory dialogue."
If you've got two hours to spare and want to be immersed into the playful imagination of a Brazilian child, check out Papo & Yo.

Final Fantasy IX, 2000
Now allow me to go a bit into detail about the game:
+The visuals are as stunning as ever, now even better with the upgraded models and cutscenes. Backgrounds remain rather blurry, though they still look good.
+Boosters provide newcomers with all the tools you could want to play through the game your way
+Some parts have been made more lenient to relieve people of frustration (Hint: Swordfight)
+Screen/Disc transitions are now nearly seamless: No more waiting 10 seconds to enter a town from the World Map.
-The menus appear to be a bit laggy, especially from the World Map.
-Battle menu sometimes blocks some animations (Damage numbers, spell visuals etc)
-Apparently the sound of defeated enemies were left out, or there is an error that causes no sound to be played when you defeat an enemy (For example, the sound when you defeat a Skeleton does not play).
-Some minigames, should you choose to go the full length, are still *slightly* hard (Hint: Jumprope)
All in all, Final Fantasy IX is a love letter to its predecessors, while remaining a very solid game in its own right. While some aspects of the remastered version are a bit annoying, such as the laggy menus, the core game is still as good now as when it was originally released.
A recommended Buy for all Final Fantasy fans and newcomers alike.

I love pinball. And when I got a 90% off coupon for Dream Pinball 3D, I read the reviews here and I knew what I was getting into. But I took it as a bit of a challenge, to see if I could actually get the game up and running and evaluate it on its own merits, or lack thereof. It wasn't very difficult to get going (who doesn't use a backup email and info for internet purposes these days anyway?, set compability mode for XP, and as an extra step I went ahead and added the .exe to DEP since I run Win 8.1). As long as you don't try to do anything fancy, like alt-tab or upload your scores or load the registration window, or exit, it's sort of stable. I didn't get any crashes during the game itself anyway.
The screen ratio is stretched in widescreen, and even though 16:9 is an option those resolutions can't be set. Nothing, it seems, can be done about that. I'd also recommend cranking down the effects since all the bloom, reflection, glass, lighting, etc. seems to do is make it really hard to see your ball whizzing around the distorted table. Also, there is no controller support, and the default key settings were oddly configured but could be changed.
There are 6 tables, they're nothing special really, but they're not the worst I've played. The play isn't anything novel for pinball, but it's got all the combos, multiball, missions, extra balls, etc. you expect from a decent table. The physics aren't really comparable to Pinball Arcade and the theming and missions aren't even in the same league as Pinball FX2, two outstanding pinball games which can be downloaded on Steam free with a single free table each. I did find it a bit easier to keep my ball alive on the Dream Pinball 3D tables than I generally do in the other pinball games, which was nice for a change of pace as a relatively novice player.
In all, I feel like I personally got my 70 cents' worth just to satisfy my own curiousity, but I can't really recommend the game unless you're a die-hard pinball fanatic and you're stuck with a 10 year-old computer you can't run anything better on. I'm probably going to throw this on an old laptop that I use for ancient DOS games since I think it will run fine with all the useless bells and whistles turned off and the screen ratio won't be an issue.

Needless to say, this obnoxiousness kind of lost its charm about midway through the game.
The big medal pinned on LISA's chest is its story and atmosphere. It is just constantly straight-up bleak and depressing the entire way through. This fits the main plotline in a very suitable way. You have to be resilient to push to the end of this game as it seems like LISA is just a neverending rollercoaster of misfortune and pain for its protagonist, Brad.
The combat system isn't really anything new or exciting. That being said it works pretty flawlessly and is intuitive. All that can really be said for it is that it doesn't take away from the narrative impact of the game, but adds to it.
I recommend LISA cautiously. It's definitely not for everybody.

Half-Life 2: Downfall is a sci-fi first person shooter mod for Half-Life 2 developed by Marnamai for the Source Engine. Taking place at some unclear point in the Half-Life timeline, you play as Gordon Freeman, physicist turned action hero, as he explores a place and then another place and than another after that.
This mod currently takes the form of a single chapter with two maps, although an additional two chapters are promised to come at some point, both being around the same length as this first one. The first chapter by itself took me about 40-50 minutes to beat on easy mode, although I'm not the best Half-Life player so you might beat it in more time than me. The levels, although short, are fairly compact, so be careful to search around for some extra items.
If you liked Half-Life 2, you're just about guaranteed to like this mod as well. It's got all the great level design Half-Life 2 trappings, although perhaps a bit too open for my tastes. Half-Life 2 tends to be a bit more linear than this and I got somewhat lost on my first attempt a while back. The level design is, though, very solid and fun to explore as well as play. Really does feel a bit like a "lost episode of Half-Life 2: Ep 2" in many ways, although the player starts completely weaponless and in a vehicle so it's unclear to me when this is meant to take place.
I do like this mod for what I got although I anticipate the future chapters and recommend you do to. Don't bother with the download quite yet, the experience leaves something to be desired.

I've never been a fan of Sonic. Granted, the only game I played was Sonic Advance, but I honestly just didn't have fun when I played it.
Well, I came across this game, I think from a webcomic. The characters looked cute and, for some odd reason, I immediately wanted to know about them. I searched the game up, took a peek at the website.
Honestly, at first, I was put off. It looks a lot like a Sonic game, and I was worried I'd end up not liking it. But they had a demo, and I still had this nagging itch, really wanting to know their stories. I can't explain it. Anyways, I tried the demo, since it was small and free, and much to my surprise, I liked it.
Not only that, within three days I decided I wanted the full game.
Maybe it was the nostalgic feeling of a 16(?)bit game, (apologies, I always forget the terms,) Maybe it was the adorable characters, or the fact that it had a weird, crazy, and laid back story, from what the description said.
So, the gameplay felt good, easy to figure out, easy to pick up and play, and yet I still figure out new combinations of moves daily. Exploring, at first, was secondary, since I wanted to hear the story most. (Then I discovered cards, and exploration in search of them has become one of my favorite parts of gameplay.) Combat was easy enough to grasp. Don't get hit, hit back until it's dead. Simple enough, except some enemies still kick my butt every time. (And talk about boss battles. Some of these, even the ones that use the same set of moves in an endless loop, are difficult enough that I'll restart a level just to collect a bunch of extra lives.)
The story is light and cutesy, lovable and, despite being so, could really bash me into the ground. The characters, adorable to look at, are also pretty cute as characters. I mean, it's no thought-provoking novel, honestly, but it's very good for what it is. I've not beaten even Lilac's campaign yet, but I'm steadily working my way there. The other two campaigns will be next on my to-do list for this game. The way it shows things from different prespectives is really neat.
The music is pretty nice too. Personally, I think it could improve, but the music is definitely good in this game. I especially like the invincible theme.
Hm. I don't think I have many complaints. There are a few glitches still, and there was one boss that, unfortunately, felt like it took more luck than skill to beat. Not looking forward to that one on later campaigns, honestly. I think my biggest complaint is the lack of a separate volume control for Music, Voice, and FX.
Anyways, I'd recommend it. It's not gonna be everyone's cup of tea, but nothing ever is. Now to get back to getting my butt kicked.

Freedom Planet is a Retro-inspired game done right! it's as though the develoupers used Doc Browns Time Machine, went back to the 90's and kidnapped various develoupment teams from Sonic, Megaman, and the game develoupers from Treasure!
Freedom Planet utilizes beautiful Sega Genesis 32 Bit sprites, all of which looks BEAUTIFUL and well detailed. the game consists of a fairly easy game controls and yes it is compatable with a Keyboard! and I've mastered it quite well. the game is fun and challanging in terms of puzzle solving, while there are some tough spots the game is fair even after you loose all of your lives you still have a fair set of continues. so incase you need more shots at Braven or that infernal Dragon, you have'll have some more tries even after Poor Lilac and Carol are killed (some in rather horrific ways if you think about it). OH! the game also has the most epic, Kick♥♥♥♥♥Soundtrack you'd ever heard and well worth buying as DLC. trust me you'll be jamming to it even in your sleep!... which... I have....
Now let's get down to the characters. each one has their own flavor and personality. and from what I understand they have some history to them. I wonder if there is ever gonna be a backstory comic later on?
Carol: a wildcat that I can't say I've played yet, but she has her own fair move set from what I can see in the videos. she even has a motorcycle that YES can drive up walls and on cealings! I KNOW RIGHT! HOW COOL IS  THAT!?
Milla: a rather cute Basset Hound. she is introduced early in the game. where she lacks in melee attacks she makes up for in mid ranged attacks with these green blob blocks and a shield. and each one can fire a short ranged blast.
Lilac: A Dragon who is yes our main character and I will admit my favorite! she has the best move set that's fun to play. as I recall She was originally gonna be a Hedgehog but was changed to be a dragon. A very wise choise In my opinion. and was the best thing they could do. while the game was originally going to be a sonic fangame, they decided to make it their own thing (though they've kept most of the style form what I can see). whoever decided to make Lilac a Dragon instead of a hedgehog is the wisest man or woman ever!
each character has their own move set and animations. when left idle they will do things. given enough time they will speak wanting you to get back to the game. though I'm unsure how far this goes. there is alot of content as well. card pick ups for the gallary that includes soundtracks, concept art, and dialog to name a few.
In Closing, I urge, No I DEMAND You get this game, it is the BEST 2D Retro inspired game! infact I will even say this is what Retro Game develoupers should strive. I hope this game grows in popularity, and maybe we might see a sequel! it may have started out as a sonic fangame, but I think it grew into a beast all it's own!

Sonic Generations is the best Sonic game we've had in years. The gameplay is fluid, the story isn't 100% awful, and the level design just feels right. In a lot of Sonic games, speed is almost punished because of obstacles they have at the end of loops or somewhere else that you need lightning fast reflexes to avoid when you are going full speed. Sonic generations almost completely does away with that. It takes the best of 2D and 3D sonic games, and combines them effortlessly. It is a sonic game, so of course, there will be glitches, and tedious sections, but it is a lot of fun. Yes, the 3D sections don't have the greatest design, and yes, they still are boost-to-win, but it is one of the most satisfying things to grind down a rail past a car at top speed. It is a load of fun, even if the story is a bit meh. I give it an 87/100, for good gameplay, (relatively) creative bosses, and bringing back the classic Sonic formula, with some new elements. It is held back by glitches and tedia, but that doesn't make it a bad game.

Final Fantasy IX, 2000
Now allow me to go a bit into detail about the game:
+The visuals are as stunning as ever, now even better with the upgraded models and cutscenes. Backgrounds remain rather blurry, though they still look good.
+Boosters provide newcomers with all the tools you could want to play through the game your way
+Some parts have been made more lenient to relieve people of frustration (Hint: Swordfight)
+Screen/Disc transitions are now nearly seamless: No more waiting 10 seconds to enter a town from the World Map.
-The menus appear to be a bit laggy, especially from the World Map.
-Battle menu sometimes blocks some animations (Damage numbers, spell visuals etc)
-Apparently the sound of defeated enemies were left out, or there is an error that causes no sound to be played when you defeat an enemy (For example, the sound when you defeat a Skeleton does not play).
-Some minigames, should you choose to go the full length, are still *slightly* hard (Hint: Jumprope)
All in all, Final Fantasy IX is a love letter to its predecessors, while remaining a very solid game in its own right. While some aspects of the remastered version are a bit annoying, such as the laggy menus, the core game is still as good now as when it was originally released.
A recommended Buy for all Final Fantasy fans and newcomers alike.

I'm only about 3 hours into this version, but I played the original for a very long time.  It may very well be my favorite Final Fantasy game.  Anyone who was worried about the quality of this port can put those worries to rest:  It's brilliant.  The character models and video scenes have received graphical upgrades that actually make them look better instead of messing with the original aesthetic.  The music has not been altered, so far as I can tell, and that is definitely for the better.  It's a great soundtrack.  It seems that everything we loved about the original game is here, and some things have been made even better.
There are some cheat options that can be enabled via the menu or by pressing certain buttons or keys on the pause screen, but these are, of course, completely optional.  Want to make the game run super fast?  That's a thing you can do.  Want all of the abilities to be learned as soon as you equip something?  You can do that, too, as well as setting your level and ability stones to max, turning off random encounters, having your battle meters always set to max, always doing 9999 damage, and maxing out your gil.  Some of these will be welcome additions for veterans who just want to run through the game again without certain things getting in their way, or even for newcomers who are having problems.  It's important to note that three of these options are not reversible:  Level/Ability stone max, gil max, and instant ability learning.  The game warns you before you activate any of those, so you won't mess things up by accident.
The only problem I've encountered has to do with controller support.  If I have my Xbox controller plugged in when the game launches, it's literally impossible to choose a menu option on the title screen due to the selection always jumping about.  Using the mouse is also a no-go.  Until this is fixed, simply launch the game without the controller connected, then plug it in and use it.
Overall, this is a 10/10 from me.  It's a great port of a fantastic game.

Today I played through Papo & Yo (Minority Media Inc.﻿), an action adventure (mostly 3D puzzle platforming) about a young boy who escapes the abuse of his alcoholic father into a surrealistic Latin American–esque slum, where he embarks on a quest to cure "Monster" of its addiction to poisonous frogs. The monster (a very clearly indicated metaphor for the protagonist's father) is both a helpful aid it surmounting obstacles and progressing through the game's environment, but also the game's only true "enemy" (when under the influence of frogs), who becomes not only a danger to others, but also the protagonist himself, who in the end discovers that there is no cure for "Monster". So, it's basically a journey of acceptance and letting go.
An enjoyable game—not very difficult, but the environments and puzzles were interesting and non–repetitive. There were occasional glitches and I had to replay one section when Monster got stuck on the environment and blocked progress, but nothing game–breaking. Notable is that the character you play as is non–White and non–Western (although there is no explicit nationality or ethnicity), and also non–English speaking (but not Spanish or Portuguese, either—some sort of constructed or conglomerate language is used in the game's limited dialog). Sad that playing as something other then a White male American is "notable", but that's how it is…

So, this game is not easy. You can run into a lot of unlucky scenarios in the unforgiving expanses of space. But, it's fun.
The premise is that you are running from people that want to catch you. This makes it so that you cannot stay still for too long. Progression in this game is moving forward through space via FTL jumps to different areas with their own things to offer. Whether they be space pirates, abandoned space stations, or shops. You make lots of little decisions as you come across things and people in the world. The goal is to reach the end point, but it is rather difficult to do so as this is a rougelike. Meaning that your first death is your last in each run. The randomization of places each time through luckily gives this game great replayability.
The crux of the gameplay is managing your spaceship (that you get to name!) and its crew as you go along in your journey. Sometimes you're forced into combat against other ships and you have to make the right strategic decisions that let you survive. Whether that means venting a room with fire in it or letting one crew member die to let the others live. The management of the spaceship is a lot of fun and throughout your journey as you go to different sectors you slowly gain enough currency to also upgrade your ship. Also, you can pick up more crew members of various species.
This is a unique gem that I think any fan of spacefaring simulation strategy in some combination will enjoy.

Hide and Shriek is a 1v1 game about two students at opposing schools being invisible and having a game afterhours.  The game play with scoring by either tricking your opponents with traps (via rigging them along the ground, doors, cabinets, etc) and by finding your invisible opponent and shrieking them, 3 shrieks in a row and you win automatically!
Each match lasts 10 minutes and all 10 of those can be filled with tense searching and hoping that your next touch isn't going to throw you across the room by a gust of wind, or that cabinet you touched might electrify you, or even that noise you heard is your invisible rival opening something right next to you unknowingly.
It's a fun little game, an added bonus if you're a fan of The Secret World in which this game has goodies for, the only downside is possibly the lower population of players further down the road after halloween.
Edit: As of late November I've found the game a bit more difficult to find players with. So having a friend to play with you would likely be the best idea!

This isn't the best Final Fantasy game. Final Fantasy 6 is the best one. But this is a VERY close second, and my personal favorite in the series. The character models and cutscenes are much more polished looking in this version, and the autosave/faster load times make this the best version I've played of this game.
The only things that bother me with this version that I've seen so far, are that the game caps at 30fps, and there is a bar on each side of the screen (at least at the resolution I have it set at for my monitor). Overall, I'd definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes the old Final Fantasy games and never got around to playing this one, OR if you just want to play the game again and relive your childhood.

The best port of the PlayStation-era FINAL FANTASY games to hit Steam. There are minor issues here and there, but in comparison to how poor the re-releases of the VII and VIII PC versions were, this game is miles above.
Audio sounds fantastic, Button prompts are changed to either Keyboard prompts or Xbox controller prompts, FMVs look beautiful. Keybinds can be rebound, mouse works just fine in menus and for movement. That's a good number of the major issues I had with FINAL FANTASY VII and FINAL FANTASY VIII Steam releases gone.
Beyond those, the issues I do have I could classify as minor or understandable, such as the lack of borderless windowed which could be forced via third party tools or the lack of having any in-game volume sliders to adjust SFX and BGM and the lack of full 360-movement even if using a controller.
The biggest issue I see people having with this port is the lack of HD backgrounds, which is a shame, but I consider completely understandable, though a number of the very original backgrounds were found (
) I don't think it's very likely or reasonable to expect Square Enix to have every single one required to be laying around somewhere and if the port team had done work on the current ones, you can bet their would be people complaining that they preferred the old versions. That being said it is a shame it causes such a rift between the model of characters and the quality of the backgrounds.
All in all I think this is almost as good as a port as you could expect from a 16 year old PS1 title where the source code has been lost.
As for the game itself? It's definitely my favorite of the PS1 era Final Fantasy games and is up there amongst my favorite Final Fantasy games when including every single one. A must play if you like Final Fantasy and haven't tried this one yet, or even simply enjoy JRPGs.

So, after careful considration, I'm going to review Freedom Planet and hopefully not sound like a huge fan girl or dweeb.
Pros:  Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥  Freedom Planet.
I refer to it as 'Sonic Cat' to almost everyone, because it takes the speed and level design nods straight from Sonic the Hedgehog (a little Google search will point you to the origins of FP, which was a Sonic-based fan game), with the attacks and beat-up stylization of many platformers of the 90s-as a dragon or a cat.  You move fast, you act fast, you can chain and cancel attacks with finesse.  It takes some getting used to-but what Sonic game didn't?  I've played as all three characters.  Lilac is hands down the best to run with-her speed isn't over the top despite being the fastest, her move set has a fantastic flow, and doesn't devolve to 'cheesy' or 'cheap' at any point.
The voice acting is actually pretty solid, and varied, as though they took some considerable time with it.
Difficulty curve is pretty standard:  early levels are great for getting used to controls, exploring, feeling out which character is best for you (Lilac is my personal favorite), complete with vivid color schemes, great soundtrack that reflects the level dynamic and game length, and increases accordingly.  Boss fights are REALLY unique.  The RoboPanther looks like a big bad straight out of MegaMan, and the entire fight scene is packed with action (and you genuinely get to particiapte!).  You'll find this true with many of the boss fights overall.
The soundtrack leaves you feeling good, or in the later levels, determined to win.  Tunes are elegant, quirky, jazzy, and fulfilling like all of your favorite 8 and 16 bit gemstones.  Seriously, listen to it in your car on the way to work-it's a great ride!
Cons:  The story is pretty cliche, very meh at best.  It's an oddity.  However, it's still stomachable.
Balance between characters is almost not there.  It's difficult to switch from Lilac to Carol to Millia, as they all have their own unique skills, but none match Lilac's even a little.  Carol has fantastic mobility, but at the cost of no double jump and lower damage ratio, and Millia is a classic glass cannon:  low health, slowest movement, can't double jump BUT does float, and hits like a truck.  Certain bosses on Lilac can be a breeze while Millia and Carol struggle slightly.
The difficulty curve, while a true curve, gets a little stupid toward the end.  Enemies make returns and gang up on you pretty bad, while still introducing new ones, and boss battles get closer to insane with each passing level.  The fourth to last boss, for example, everyone has to fight across their respective storyline...but if you aren't careful on Lilac, or worse aren't playing her, there are moves that can cover the entire screen that you can't avoid and just eats your health.  It can get frustrating.
That said, I've beat the game with Lilac, am in the final stages with Carol, and on the third to last stage with Millia.  It's doable-but it will test your patience.
Overall:  snag this game.  It's a great ride through nostalgia land with new faces, great music, fun gameplay, and replayability Sonic hasn't seen since Sonic and Knuckles.  You won't be disappointed.

This game is absolute fun.  If you loved playing Sonic the Hedgehog on Sega Genesis as a kid, this will bring back some good memories, and give new ones at the same time.  The game mechanics and controls are pretty solid.

Now some people seem to complain about the voice acting being terrible, but I do not.
Galaxy Trail isn't a triple-A studio that can throw hundreds of thousands at voice acting.  I wouldn't want them to either.  I find the voice acting to be on par with the characters, and gives them proper personality.  The story and plot seems good and decent and hopefully it does get expanded upon as well in the future DLC that was announced.  It would be nice to learn more about the events that unfolded before Torque and Lord Brevon showed up, as well as more about the Red Scarves.
The music and sound effects?  Quite good.  I love the effort that was put into the music.  Most stages are split in two sections separated by a minor boss fight, and the music gets changed up to a slightly different theme.  It just all fits well with the mood.
You will love this game.  11/10.
Aaaaand if the voice acting really bothers you, the game does have a 'Classic' option that includes no story element scenes.

For the life of me, I have no idea why this game has such good reviews. I'm gonna break it down piece-by-piece.
The story is mediocre. First off, it's too short, and can be completed in less than 12 hours. The entire story is "you've been betrayed, now go kill him" and then "the guy who just ordered you to kill the guy that betrayed you just betrayed you, now go kill him." You spend half the game just trying to fix the mistakes that your character makes. There's no development, just go place to place to place, shoot, kill, credits. There is not a SINGLE noteworthy plot twist, and 75% of the characters aren't around for long enough to even care about. The protagonist is laregly uninteresting; he's the cliche "I did this for good reasons, but then I found out people die when you shoot them." There's no gravity to the story; it lacks any sort of impact.
The ending is TRASH. There is absolutely no closure.
The graphics are adequate, they do what they need to do, no complaints.
I only encountered one visual bug, and my game never crashed. Good job there.
Now, the gameplay. The gunplay is awful and prehistoric, and the enemies have incredibly inconsistent aim unless they are up close, at which point they wreck you. You die INCREDIBLY easily on the standard difficulty, and the game has horribly inconsistent checkpoints which will set you back 10-15 minutes at times, probably a way to pad the game for additional length. Cars are fun to drive, but nothing special. The police are one of the most annoying mechanics of this game. They will chase you for speeding. That's all you need to know. Again, another mechanic to add time to the game because you have to run everytime a cop sees you go 50 down the highway. You can press a button to limit your speed so you never get in trouble for that, but then it takes considerably more time to get places. That would be fine and all if there was an incentive to explore the world, but there really isn't
The setting, a decent part of the game. One thing that this game got right was the size of the game world. It is VERY small, which is a refreshing change from all of these AAA open-world games with huge worlds that have nothing to discover. Everything is relatively condensed, and it's nice. The city the game takes place in is completely generic with no memorable locations. The time period it's set in complements the game well but games like L.A. Noire do it better.
Weak and short story, weak characters, lacking gameplay, decent setting. Again, I don't understand why this game is so positively reviewed. It could have been so much better than it was

Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing

TL;DR - highly recommended!
Possibly one of the best RTS's I've played and, in my opinion, a great improvement over the first (though this is subject to intense debate :P ). Both games retain the same elements which truly make for a great game!
The scale of the gameplay is perfect, not too large to make individual units insignificant, and not too small to feel like you're playing Commando's.
The synergy of the different units means that units purchased at the start of the match still retain usefulness right up until the end. The unit roster offers a selection of viable strategies which result in a diversity of gameplay which is often lacking in other games. It's a game which is deep, and takes time to truly master.
The cover system is a wonder, and the fog of war makes for interesting game play and ambushes. The way resources are generated through map control make this a strategically interesting game with reasons for actually holding ground.
Arguably one of the more frustrating elements, but also one which makes it one of the more interesting games is the random element of combat. Chance turns this into a game of calculated risk over simply rock/paper/scissors. The tension added because you're never really sure how an encounter will play out can be one of the most satisfying or frustrating moments, but really adds to the game.
To address the accusations of Lootboxes and DLC - the game does include "lootcrates", but it is not possible to buy them. You do not get duplicates - instead you get ingame currency to buy the bulletins or commanders you didn't receive. All of these "lootcrate" items are available without paying any real world money. I don't believe that this is the best system to unlock items, but they have addressed complaints to a degree which I find satisfying. I believe that the additional factions are worth what they're being sold for. This game is being supported to this day and I feel that the money that I have spent on this game is well worth it. I don't feel exploited, or that this is a pay to win system.
All these elements (and probably others that I haven't mentioned) come together in a great way, which is why there's still a community surrounding this game years after its original release! I couldn't recommend it more.

I'm finally happy to be able to play again this game I dropped too early at the time.
If you're reading Steam reviews you're probably searching for an answer to the crucial question:
So, here's a few notes about that:
- The game runs on the original frame rate, i.e. 30fps in towns and 15fps in battle, world map and cutscenes. It's not a big deal once you get used to it once again, but it's a shame they couldn't find a way to improve on the original.
- It is made in Unity engine, which means that having your controller work with it can be really painful.
- Graphics are a mixed bag: 3D models are very beautiful looking, but the blurry 2D backgrounds meld very bad with the models and are often downright confusing.
- Overall the game isn't CPU/GPU intensive at all; it will probably run well on any potato even on integrated graphics.
- Music is the original one and not a remix. It sounds as good as ever.
- They added 7 boosters that can be very helpful to ease the suffering on the hardest parts.
- It has some very minor bugs like inputs not correctly displayed in some parts or dialogues randomly freezing before they start back again. I didn't find anything game breaking, but I'm still too early in the game to judge on that.
- It still has Tetra Master. AND 3 achievements for playing it. Yuck.

"A diamond in the rough" is the first thought that came to mind when i played my first session of this game. Personally this game first came to my attention while watching H2o delirious (great lad would recommend) and from there on had to have a go at it. The game itself is a 1v1 first person online multiplayer horror were players assume the role of two high school students from Miskatonic's estranged sister school of Innsmouth high during Halloween night in a twisted magical game of something akin to hide and seek. Each player is invisible to one another and objectively must attempt to acquire their coloured orbs of blue or red and deliver it to their periodically moving altar all the while avoiding, countering and entrapping their enemies with magical game changing runes scattered around the map. To win players must by the end of the countdown or jump scare their opponent 3 times in a row, have accumulated more points plus the additional bonuses than their opposition.
Story/character Development: Like with any funcom game, the narrative background of this particular game is set in the same universe as funcom's MMO The secret world, with several allusions to the TSW around the map and in the lore. Evidently the narrative of the game itself is more or less what you would expect in a 1v1 online game. I  love the premise of the story and how it sets the frame of mind for the game. There is just something about two students from what would be the equivalent of what would be Hogwarts but with a contemporary twist, getting up to mischief on Halloween that appeals to me. Maybe it is the inner lore lover i am or the many references to the other games of funcom i have so many fond memories of. The developers clearly thought out the background for the game and its implementation into the actual game play. The many background stories of how the mystical runes came to be or the various brief but intriguing references to characters from TSW that helps build their background.
3.5/5
Replay Value: Moving on from my reminiscence and into the actual quality of the game, the replay value is somewhat abundant. The basics of the game are the same in every round, find orb, find altar, place orb on alter and earn points to stay ahead of your opponent. The runes however are what make this game truly special. With around 10 unique spells all with different opportunities to ♥♥♥♥ with your class mate and not to mention the additional spells created from combining certain runes, this game gleefully presents you with about 30 different ways to scare and hinder your opponent or protect you from them. I must admit i get a buzz at leap frogging around the map every time i find a hopscotch rune. Never the less it is the unique situations presented in each game that make this one something to pick up again and again. I for instance encountered one fellow who wouldn’t stop leaving decoy exploding orbs for me to find or another time when i encountered a player who had a knack for throwing fireballs. Another addition is the levelling system used to unlock certain items that will be mentioned in customization. Some people probably think that on top of everything a levelling system is stupid however I disagree, it is this very levelling system I have found that can be an incentive to come back and play again. But the biggest absolute blue balls thing about this game is the map. More maps is a must for a game like this if it is to stay afloat.
3.5/5
Gameplay and controls: The true gem of this game is its gameplay and although clunky, its controls are simple and clear to understand. The game provides a repetitive basis goal so that players clearly understand what they have to do but also uses the game changing runes to combat any boredom the player might encounter. Its abundance of spells to screw over the opposition and the individually customised jumps cares are what make this game so enjoyable yet simple as to understanding your goal. The actual controls of the game are clunky to be blunt, with high motion blurs and a sort of swaying as you walk all of which can be changed from settings. But the consistent clicking and holding just to open doors and cupboards can defiantly leave you with a sore hand after a few games.
4/5
Graphics: I almost forget that funcom is actually a pretty wealthy company sometimes because of the below average fan base and little advertising I see of it, so going into this game I expected somewhat of a bare minimum of graphical quality but oh boi am I glad I was proven wrong. This game is beautifully designed in its spliced magical high school aesthetic, everything drawn and textured in detail. Sure it’s not as realistic looking as people would like it to be but that is exactly what fits the game itself. Its entirety is based on a wacky game two kids play WITH MAGIC. It isn’t meant to look as if it was a real place because it was built not to be. It was designed to look fun and mysterious, to appeal to that inner child of ours back when our imaginations ran rampant and magical school games like this, for us at least, existed. So some people might disagree with me here and I realise that as the game grows it will look better but from what I see now the developers are on the right track.
4/5
Character customization: I am so glad that they included a feature like this into the game and although sometimes it can seem like a very small feature, it’s always enjoyable to be scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at the abominations other players have created. The entire customization mechanic for the game revolves around the jumps scares you use to catch your opponent. A singular head model with a variety of 10 default heads to choose from, mixed in with different laughs and voices plus 18 different decorations PER-HEAD it’s gonna be one hell of a night. The only catch? The levelling system. You unlock one customization option per level you level up which again is an incentive to play again which I agree with. Overall I always like it when i get to see other people’s creations on screen and what I could possibly do with my own to scare others. In conjunction with the runes, it adds a refreshing aspect to the game with its basic repetitive plays sometimes.   3.5/5
Co-op and Online Multiplayer: The real kick in the balls aspect about this game. Taking into consideration that it is very new so there hasn’t been a lot of time for people to join, the amount of people that play this game are sparse to few. If this game is to survive it needs more players, something which can, given funcoms fan base, be a major problem. Obviously they have got some popular youtubers to advertise it and steam advertisement is also good but please for the love of god it needs a bigger player base if it’s going to continue. Waiting times can be a killer (don’t worry I found a fix for those of you who know what im talking about), but the ping you get is actually decent and trust me this is coming from a guy who gets (if im luck) 600kb/s speed tops.
3.5/5
(Pro tip: to shorten wait times make sure u are connected to NA region in the games options and change your download region on steam settings to Washington DC, make sure u change back to your region tho when downloading new games or when you finish playing)
Final thoughts and review: it’s not often you find a game like this and I highly recommend it. My only recommendations for this game is its expansion on maps and possibly runes and spells to keep people interested, maybe a few game modes to spice up the basics would also attract a lot of players back for more and for Christ sakes more advertising not just for the developers but for the players as well. So many good games have failed on the basis that their wasn’t a big enough player base and I pray to Cthuhlu (pun intended) that doesn’t happen to this game so share and recommended this please to anyone you might think would be interested.

NO SPOILERS.
You're Vito Scaletta. War Hero, just getting off to Empire Bay. Your home. Where everyone you care about is there. Your sister, mother, and importantly, your crazy friend Joe.
Turns out your old man took out some money from a loan shark before he died. That's where Joe comes in, your closest and most trustworthy friend. He is involved in some "shady" circumstances, but being the person you are, you don't really care. And so, begins your quest to rise up- and eventually join the mafia. An elite criminal organization, hell-bent on getting what they want, when they want, all with a sense of mystique and class.
In mafia 2, you play a charismatic and unforgiving character, Vito. The writing in this game is great. Sure, there does have to be a bit of suspension of disbelief, and if you over think the story, you'll probably think it doesn't always add up. But if you don't think and you just play the game, you'll realize how witty and clever it truly is. The characters are funny, and they are a joy to listen to them interact with one another. They are clever, and although the game has dirty jokes, it still pulls it off with a sense of style and finesse, needed in a game like mafia 2.
The combat is fun and engaging, and it isn't too easy, or too simple. The fisticuffs or "hand to hand", combat is basically quick punches and hard punches, but you can pull off combo moves and counters to really ruin your enenies day. The gunplay is nothing incredibly difficult. There's a pretty good cover system, and if you are attuned to playing any 3rd person view games, you'll get the gist. Fighting in both retrospects feels fun and exciting. I always found myself hiding behind cover, or running to get into it. That way I don't die for another bazillion times. (I played on medium. Considering I am not always the best shot, I missed a lot. And I died A LOT. But I can admit my defeat.)
I recommend playing on medium if you'd like a plausible and good challenge. The best thing I think about this was the characters and the variety of missions. That is not to say there weren't a few repetitive missions. There were a lot. But there were also a lot that stood out as their own, as you risk your neck for the characters you grow to care deeply for.
My biggest complaint is this- the driving was awful. I used a mouse and keyboard, so maybe I was at a disadvantage. But it was like I was on slippery ice all the time. And it made racing to get somewhere, or trying to stop a car incredibly frustrating. But this is honestly my biggest complaint. And I can't say anything else about it because it was so engaging and enjoyable.
The storyline is where the game gets you. It's funny, witty, clever. And at times, dark, gloomy and ominous. It pulls you in and doesn't leave your mind. Especially the ending as--
Got you.
Overall, I recommend mafia 2. Especially if you are looking for a story driven game with a nice GTA esque open world, an awesome storyline, great and memorable characters and moments and action. Just don't expect to be driving in the grand prix in this.
Thanks for reading! And I look forward to Mafia 3!  Over and out.

1 When I was growing up, you were either a Mario kid or a Sonic kid and I was firmly in Team Sonic.
The original Megadrive classic was such a fast and fun game and it really taught me how to play games. It taught me everything I needed to know and prepared me for a life of gaming.
Finally, after a few mediocre games, Sonic is back in form!
Sonic Generations starts with our favourite blue blur on his way to his surprise birthday party where all his friends have gathered to celebrate. But storm clouds are on the horizon in the form of an unknown force that has something to do with time.
Before he can even finish his chilli dog, the time monster kidnaps all of Sonics friends!
Sonic must journey into different sections of his past and restore them to the original timeline in order to rescue his friends.
I found the lack of Archie comic characters such as Sally Acorn and Mighty the Armadillo disappointing.  I especially missed Lara-Su, as she has a lot to do with time travel alongside Silver in the Sonic universe.
I find the lack of these characters a little bit sad, especially as its Sonics birthday...
Despite that little complaint, I'm perfectly happy with the plot and characters used.  The game is a lot of fun and the characters that do feature are interesting.
It’s not a super complex story, but the developers did an excellent job creating an interesting narrative with twists and turns at every corner. It’s a great, back to basics story that treats Sonic with a solid amount of respect.
Very quickly you find yourself in the first section of the hubworld called Limbo.
It serves as a gateway to nine different story missions which have two play styles, thanks to the ability to swap between modern sonic and his classic 1990's Megadrive / Genesis variant.
As Classic Sonic, you play in the familiar 2D side scrolling platformer style, breaking item boxes, jumping ledges and speeding your way around newly designed worlds from Sonic’s past.
As Modern Sonic, you play through the world in a 3D platformer style, which is much faster and has a lot more to dodge and swerve through.
Each level is quite short but you may find this is a good thing.  If you haven’t played a lot of the previous Sonic the Hedgehog games, you will probably die often!  There is a little bit of a learning curve initially.
Just like Sonic Adventure 2, as soon as you’re out of lives, you’re all the way back to the start of that level. However, that’s what I love about Sonic, you have to die a few times so you can learn where you need to jump, or what is the best path is to take. Each time you progress a little further and you really do feel that satisfied when you finally reach the end goal ring.
Sonic has always been about speed and getting a continuous run going and Sonic Generations is no exception!
Speed is the element that can cause some very intense moments, particularly in the 3D levels when you need to build up your speed to evade a G.U.N truck from squishing you, or escape a crumbling building.
As you progress through the story, you will unlock various challenges.  This is where you’ll get to interact with Sonic’s friends by either racing them to the finish line or enlisting their help in order to complete a challenge.
You don’t have to complete all of these courses to finish the game but it is a great way to collect more rings and use them to level up.
The upgrades you can buy include more sure footing and faster sneakers, which help on the later, more difficult levels.
If you’re feeling particularly nostalgic, collecting enough rings will also allow you to play Sonic on an unlockable Sega Mega Drive Emulator. This brought back many memories for me. I thought this was a really nice little touch and a nice way for the developers to almost say thank you to the fans for sticking with this franchise and character for so long.
Visually, Sonic has never looked so good.  The remastered worlds really glow full of colour and depth as you zoom past. And when you first hear those classic themes remixed, it made me feel like a 90's kid all over again.
If you have been playing Sonic for the past 20+ years, you’ll fully appreciate his sense of humour which makes several references to just how crazy some of his earlier adventures got, which I got a bit of a kick out of.
It’s almost like the writers were saying “Yeah, we know the previous games weren’t that great either, so let’s just poke fun at them instead”.
I found the lack of Archie Comic references to characters such as Sally Acorn very sad, as this game was the perfect opportunity to include them in a "Alternate Timeline" story.
But thankfully, that’s what mods are for, and there are quite a few huge mods for Sonic Generations!
Ever wanted to play as Donald duck and have Goofy (A reskin of Silver) throw things at you in a boss battle?
Ever wanted to play as Sally Acorn through a level from Sonic Unleashed?
Well now you can and thanks to the "Sonic Hacking Contest", there are hundreds of mods made every year!
The mods will certainly extend your playtime for hours...
I had a blast with this game and I think I probably enjoyed it as much as Sonic colours for the Wii.
I think the game shows that Sonic is back in form, and he has returned to the glorious days I remember from my childhood.
Of course you’ll appreciate it much more if you’re a long-time fan of the series, but even if you’re new to Sonic, it won’t take too long to be drawn into his world.
I found the lack of Archie comic characters being at Sonic’s party such as Sally Acorn a little bit sad, but overall, it’s a solid instalment for such a legendary character.  I enjoyed playing the game immensely.

I will always keep The Secret World close to my heart. Funcom's MMORPG is basically my first. Alright, I did play a bunch of them even before realizing TSW exists, but I didn't enjoy any of them on the same scale I've enjoyed TSW. The only reason why I am not currently playing The Secret World are daily life obligations.
But enough about TSW.
Apart from The Park and The Black Watchmen, Hide and Shriek is third TSW spin-off. It's a devious, multiplayer take on hide'n'seek in The Secret World. Hide and Shriek is two player multiplayer game where players need to score as many points as possible by collecting colorful orbs or end a game instantly by scaring their opponent three times in a row.
But it ain't gonna be easy - simply because both players are invisible.
And here's simple, yet powerful concept worthy of slow and thunderous applause. Why didn't anyone think of that earlier? So how do you know your opponent is somewhere near? The only way you will be able to recognize your opponent's presence is witnessing changes and interactions. If you see the doors opening or colorful orbs levitating, you know your enemy is there. Remember that awesome scene with ghosts and babies from "The Frighteners"? That's what I'm talking about.
But things get more complicated then that. First of all, camping is basically a no-no, because it would be pretty easy to stalk near someone's altar (place to drop your orbs and earn points) and scare them while they're approaching. Altars vanish when you place your orb on them or after some time to stop people from camping. Players can also collect various runes. These runes can be used to place traps on objects or floor, summon haunting demons or curses. Even better, you can easily combine various runes and create more powerful spells that will reveal your opponent or make you hunt him down with precision. But, you must be asking... does that mean players can aim to create the most powerful spell in the book? Well yes... if the random rune picker at the beginning of the match allows you to.
It's easy to scare your friends - once Shriek-o-Meter (I've made this up, please continue using it so one day I end up in game credits) has been filled, you will be able to scare the other player by pressing Spacebar when you're near and facing him/her. If you miss, your Shriek-o-Meter will drain and you will be visible for a few seconds, giving a chance to your enemy to scare you. If you get scared, a jumpscare will stop your heart for a few moments. It consists of loud sound and 90's Halloween influenced 'deadhead'. Of course, the effect is stronger when you're playing the game with headphones and not expecting to be scared, e.g. in situation when your opponent sees you or perform an ambush in unexpected situations.
Matches last for ten minutes and tend to be pretty tense. Hide and Shriek forces players to move and eventually make mistakes that other players will notice. It is not scary game nor it tends to be - it is supposed to be funny and devilish take on hide and seek and it works so damn well with its Goosebumps aesthetics.
Hide and Shriek is definitely a spin-off game and a damn good one, but I don't think Funcom is really aware of what beast they have created. With its progression and unlockables, it will keep the players busy for some time, but Funcom should really consider making it something more than digital sideshow attraction. More levels, masks, spells, multiplayer options and game modes could definitely launch Hide and Shriek to indie stardom. Let's keep our fingers crossed and hope Funcom will realize it themselves.

Quick Summary: Small open world game with an engaging story, though the gunplay is mediocre. The game is very story driven so despite the fact that you can drive all over the city, you can’t really “do” anything (no significant side quests or minigames). Still, it’s definitely worth playing.
You play Vito Scalletta, a World War 2 vet come home early from the Italian front, with connections to organized crime in the city. You don’t want to break your back working for chump change like your father, so you turn to petty crime, making friends in low places. The story takes place over at least a decade so you experience the various highs and lows of joining a criminal enterprise, though interestingly I don’t remember the word “mafia” being used significantly. Instead, you throw your allegiance behind one of 3 “families” running the crime in the city of Empire Bay. As you’d expect among a bunch of crooks, the families aren’t satisfied with sharing the city, and underworld war is coming.
The game is played in third person perspective similar to Sleeping Dogs or Grand Theft Auto, and just like those games, you’ll be spending a lot of time in cars driving around the city. Being that the game takes place in the mid 1900’s the cars aren’t that fast so it actually takes some time to travel around. Also, the city’s main highway isn’t very well developed, so once you get on, you kind of have to follow it to the end (no exits along the way). As I mentioned earlier, the game city isn’t all that large, and there’s not too much to do other than search for collectibles. Unlike the Saint’s Row games, there are very few diversions to spend your time on, although you can rob the few stores in the city for some easy money (don’t bother). Causing trouble (like robbery or running people over) will get the cops on you, but most of the time you can just outrun them and they’ll forget you exist.
Combat in the game uses a regenerating health meter and you only have a few guns to choose from. Generally I found the semi-auto pistols easier to get headshots with, and you hide behind cover for protection while waiting for your health to refill. There is a little hand to hand combat, but it’s very simple (light punch, Heavy punch, and Dodge) and mostly used for story based fights. Most of your regular fighting will be with guns.
Pros:
+Very interesting story, with characters you can get invested in.
+Spend some time with the collectible nudie mags
Cons:
-The game has an unusual check point save system where it doesn’t really save your progress unless you progress on the main story. That means if you spend a lot of time out in the city trying to make money and get killed by cops, you’ll very likely lose everything you gained since the last story checkpoint.
-The game DLC’s are no longer being sold on Steam at this time.
Overall, the game is definitely worth a playthrough. Don’t bother trying to hoard up money because you don’t really have anything to spend it on other than a couple of car upgrades.

Papo & Yo is a puzzle game, however that is also where it fails the hardest. The puzzles in the game seem to be designed in such a way to waste as much of your time as possible, not because they're difficult (which none of them actually are), but because of the massive amount of running around that is required for solving each and every single one of them.
The second major fault of the game is the clunky way of trying to control the monster to do what you want him to do, the mechanic is contrived, again simply to add to the play time.
The storyline is very thin, the game tries to allude to things, however everything is already blatantly clear long before the conclusion of the game. And the soundtrack is almost equally nonexistant, most of the time there is no background music playing at all and the rest of time it's only sometimes interesting.
All in all Papo & Yo Desperately tries to be much more clever than it actually is.
However despite all its faults the game had me mildly entertained throughout, the atmosphere it tried to create was enough for me to finish the game, and because of the short play time and more importantly without any major setbacks there was nothing stopping me from doing so.

I just finished my first playthrough of Freedom Planet. I'm not sure  if I'm going to 100% it, but I'm definitely going to at least beat it with every character. Let me just say, this game hit me so hard, and right in the childhood too. I knew going in that this would be a nostalgia trip, with it being a spiritual successor to the Genesis Sonic games, (first games I ever played as a wee lad) but what I wasn't ready for was all the quiet homages to other great Genesis games, such as Ristar, Alex Kidd, and even a little Vectorman! This game was a pleasure to play as somebody who grew up with these games, but I feel like the game totally stands on it's own at the same time. It introduces enough fresh new ideas to where it feels like a respectful homage to the Genesis, as opposed to a blatant recycling of old ideas. It never relies on the nostalgia either, and I think that's what made it such a great game. And don't get me started on all those epic boss fights... so many of them... and they were all so good! I give it a 4 out of 5, only because the dialogue is cheesy at times, and the voice acting could be better, but the characters were no less memorable because of it.
Sega could learn a lot from this game.

This game is a MUST HAVE for anyone that's into side-scrolling super hyperactive platformers. Needless to say, Freedom Planet draws a huge inspiration from the early Sonic The Hedgehog games but as they say, imitation is the best form of flattery. The programmers behind Freedom Planet manage to take the core gameplay elements of classic Sonic games while still keeping their game unique and even original. This game isn't exactly like Sonic though, different characters have different mechanics, like Carol isn't as focused on speed as Lilac, so instead her levels focus a little more on combat kind of similar to a beat em-up kind of platformer. Not only is the gameplay fantastic but the characters each have their own distinct personalities and characteristics which enriches the gameplay even more. Another big thing this game is focused on, if not the biggest thing, is the story. If you go into the story with the mindset of looking for some kind of super depth and complexity then STOP right now. The story isn't bad and it isn't super great but it's something that really ENTICES the gameplay and sets you into the mood more. There are cutscenes that last up 10 minutes, so it makes completing levels more rewarding and the BOSS battles are just insane!!! I CANT REMEMBER taking on bosses this EPIC! The bosses are challenging but also the animation and sequences into the boss battles are just spec-♥♥♥♥ING-tacular. NOW I KNOW that you're tired of me rambling on and on about this game but if you really want a GREAT 2D platforming experience ESPECIALLY if you miss the glory gameplay of Sonic The Hedgehog series, then this game IS For YOU!! Buy it and support it. There's a reason why this game is coming to PS4 and Wii U/3Ds eShop. IT'S JUST THAT GOOD!
