Did you ever play the Genesis as a kid? Or ever play a decent sonic game? Or rocket knight?
Then you'll love Freedom Planet. It's a 'retro'(and I use the term only to describe the aesthetic, the gameplay has depth and a pleasurable console-feel that's not boring or re-hashed) game with old Sega aesthetics and interesting mechanics on every level. There are multiple characters to play, time attack modes, speed run attempts, etc., and a surprisingly long story mode for such a small studio. A good comparison is Shovel Knight, only Freedom planet is an homage to old Genesis games rather than old nintendo staples.
Freedom Planet features intense, fast paced gameplay that follows its own internal old-game logic(you can run up and down sheer walls as long as you have the speed, rotate around large loops ala sonic, etc.), a refreshingly simple combat system, and almost every enemy is entirely unique in sprite and animation. There are numerous mini bosses, a large stable of end-stage bosses, and a ton of beautifully rendered stages to run around in, each of which are huge, sprawling, and give you the 'freedom' to zoom around in almost any direction.
The story has a very weird saturday-morning-but-adult vibe, with brightly colored characters and voice acting work that feels almost purposefully over the top and ham-y. It's a bit surprising how dark the story gets while maintaining a relatively child-like atmosphere. Some of the cutscenes do drag on, but there's an option to run the game sans cutscenes if all you want is to have fun and run the game again for time or simply just don't care about a story at all.
There are a lot of nice, professional polish touches to Freedom Planet. Many Bosses have cutscenes, but if you die you simply respawn a bit further back, and whne you approach the Boss they leap right into the combat without having to redo dialogue again.There are a ton of secrets, and everything is bright and well animated in lots of primary colors.  The game's pacing is frantic, but in a way that feels fun rather than rushed. Every level feels different in a good way, with new mechanics added almost before you've learned the last stage's unique playability.
It does have some problems though. Some might find the deviant-art-esque characters unappealing from an aesthetics point, and the dialogue can sometimes be cringeworthy. And certain environmental effects are instant-kills, which can be tempo-ruining, pulling you out of the game. However, these are all minor concerns in what is a surprising gem of a game that should please any of thsoe nostalgic for a game that plays start to finish with a satisfying saturday-morning-cartoon power of friendship storyline.

The first thing people are going to do when they see this game is compare it to Sonic.  Is this a fair justification?  Yes, and only if you're willing to admit that there are people who make better Sonic games than Sega.  There are two ways to play Freedom Planet.  Story mode, complete with cutscenes, fantastic voice acting, and of course the gameplay, and arcade mode which plays like any 2D Adventure game from the Sega Genesis days.  So just what makes this game so damn fun?
First of all, it controls well.  If you're going to have characters platform and do it quickly, they need to be able to control well.  The only thing to say about this is.....NAILED IT.  Yup, the multiple(did I mention that yet?) characters each control very well and navigate through the levels very well.  Taking a nod back to the classic sonic games, each character has their own quirk if you will that will allow them to traverse the level differently, which can lead to different encounters, and more importantly different gameplay mechanics leading to a ridiculously high replay value. Furthermore, the game switches nicely between speed segments, platforming, lite puzzle solving, and combat to keep you interested the whole time.  On top of all this cake, we have the icing, which is very well done boss battles.
I am giving this game a lot of praise because I haven't had this much fun with a 2D platformer like this since Sonic 3 & Knuckles.  So, it's been a while.  I love this game and want nothing more than to share with you one of the finest creations this decade.  Freedom Planet gets nothng less than a perfect score.

Akin to Shovel Knight, which pays homage to the glory of NES games, Freedom Planet is considered one of the finest tributes to Genesis titles. It is said to be a combination of Sonic, Rocket Knight, Ristar and Gunstar Heroes (none of which I've actually played, to be honest).
Being a Sonic fangame in the very beginning, Freedom Planet obviously resembles it the most, but mind you, this is not some kind of knock off. Its mechanics mix the elements of speed, combat and exploration in such a way, that you are free to be a runner, fighter or explorer and change your style at your heart's desire.
In the core mechanics we have a traditional health system, an actual combat system with a variety of moves and some very forgiving physics that does not aim to hinder your progress, so that you are able to climb any wall as long as your speed is not below walking. Sometimes physics behave really weird to the point that you might think that it is glitching (I'm looking at you, girder see-saw!), but such occurences are very rare and do not lead to anything harmful.
The level design offers wide stages, often with multiple paths, and without areas that force you to halt your movement for long. Almost every stage introduces some new element that adds enough diversity to make it feel fresh but not totally different. Graphics is colorful and very well made.
It is very worth noting, that the game has no such "pleasant" things as random bottomoless pits and wide rows of instakill spikes. Seeing an instakill contraption occurs as often as holidays, and the rare presence of pits is absolutely justified, plus the latter can be easily avoided if you apply just a little common sense and careness. So death here never feels cheap.
Another thing deserving mentioning is the lack of yet another traditional staple of running and platforming games - the contact damage. Enemies need to actively attack you to harm you (unless they are covered with spikes or fire). The resulting effect greatly helps the flow, no need to fear that you'll stop dead after colliding with some baddie - they won't stop your running.
Movement and combat feel very fluid and responsive, platforming does not induces frustration, and the boss fights - with lots of shapes and sizes, Treasure style - are sure to make your heart beating. Currently there are 3 charming playable characters (with 2 more coming at the end of summer with a free DLC), and all of them are so different, that the only thing they have in common is physics. But you'll have to find out their controls on your own, so if you feel like your character is missing something (
) don't be ashamed to look in one of the guides.
So, the game also has a story and full voice acting. Story mode tells the plot mostly through cutscenes between levels. I don't mind these, but for a lot of people they might break the pace (the longest cutscene racks up to 12 minutes). Naturally, not everyone will like these. If you are going for it, then I'd suggest you to relax and follow it like a cartoon of some sorts. Keep in mind, that with these cheesy dialogs and cute and pretty looks, the story is not all sunshine and bunnies, you might be surprised how fast things can get a downer turn. And I'm very pleased to see a dangerous villain that does not f**k around for once. Also, the narrative is mostly focused on your selected character, so you'll miss some plot points on your first playthrough.
Voice acting is fairly competent, considering that a sizeable part of the cast are either amateurs or do VA as a hobby. I find the voices mostly fitting, not inducing cringe or annoyance. To each their own though. If you do not want to see any dialogue or story stuff, there is a Classic mode, that skips it altogether. The sounds feel just right, and the music perfectly fits this kind of genre.
The last thing I want to mention is the extra little things, that are not necessary, even excessive, but present. From collectibles, to some level elements that you suprisingly can interact with, to the unique animations for hidden blooper dialogs! These all show how developers love their game.
If you feel interested after reading this, then you can check the demo available on the dev's site
(some sprites and sound are obsolete and old bugs may be present).
Overall, Freedom Planet feels like a hidden gem, sadly unnoticed or dismissed for various reasons. Personally, I thoroughly enjoyed it and give it all of my "YES!". And if you are looking for a fun high-speed platforming game (or even if you are missing those early days of Sonic), then have a look at this game - it NEEDS your attention.

A love letter to classic Sega Genesis games. What started as a Sonic the Hedgehog fan game quickly spin dashed into its own breed of hectic platforming action. The different characters you play as each have unique play styles that completely change the wonderfully created stages you race through. The soundtrack is also fantastic, and really helps bring the world to life. The voice acting is a bit cheesy, and the later boss fights are very frustrating, but the overall experience is unaffected by its stumbles. A fun ride all through out.

This game is absolutely brimming with fast paced action, awesome boss fights, better and more interesting characters than the games it pulls inspiration from, and an amazing soundtrack to boot. Fans of retro games and Sonic the Hedgehog will find much to love here, as I was surprised by the great if simple story, charming characters and solid controls. I even enjoyed the fully voiced cutscenes inbetween each level. Those who don't care for the story can play "Classic" mode which ties all the levels together with no cutscenes to get in the way of the fun. With multiple characters that genuinely play differently from each other and multiple modes, theres just too much good stuff in this game.
If I had any complaints it would be that the levels are a little too large sometimes, as I occasionally got lost and wasn't sure where to go. In addition there are some severe difficulty spikes when it comes to the boss fights. Some boss fights I'll lose 10 lives to, and then the next boss I beat in a single try.
However none of this changes the fact that this is one of my absolute favorite games and I'm not kidding when I say it's better than the vast majority of the Sonic the Hedgehog games its inspired by. Play it!

This game has a very steep learning curve and it is constantly changing in tactics and strategies almost weekly. If your a new player you can feel like your being dropped into the deep end and well you kind of are with this game. "But the more I play the better I should get" your probably thinking and this is partly true but the fact that this game has been out for sometime and is a home to veteran players since launch the chances of you even lasting long enough to 'figure' this game out before you destroy your monitor out of the sheer rage this game can bring out of you at times is little to none.
The community is 50/50 in the sense that some people will be friendly and actually try to help you out and teach you a better way of playing, what to build, what not to build and when to build it. On the other side of the fence the community can be a very aggressive and unfriendly place to new players or to players who are not that good at the game resulting in it being near impossible to join in a casual game without being kicked instantly because you are not of a certain skill level, and this bar is set incredibly high. This has been a proplem since the first installment of the franchise. A problem which at this point there is nothing the developers can really do anything about.
I really do hold this franchise a special place in my heart but because of all these overwhelmingly negative factors in place I cannot possibly reccomend this game to those who do not already have a understanding of these types of games, some patience and a cool head. This is a game like no other and is worth a buy when on sale, but it is a harsh and unforgiving game also, so tread carefully, and try keep that monitor in one piece if you should decide to purchase this game.

I had to write a review for this game. Why you ask? Well the story begins in... (lets skip this part) and that's why I love Sonic.
Now that you know the story of why I love Sonic and how much he meant to me and my childhood, I'll tell you why you should get this game: IT'S AMAZING! Did you like the good old 2D Sonic? GET IT! The game has all the nostalgia factor you need with its 2D component AND you can install classic levels through modding. Did you like the good 3D Sonic games? GET IT! The 3D levels in this game are amazing! Reviewers will say they don't live up to the 2D sections but to me they're the best part of the game and quite frankly THE BEST SONIC LEVELS I HAVE EVER PLAYED. And I've played every single Sonic game that matters except Colors (which I hear is good too). The 3D levels are the defenition of what Sonic games should be: if you're good you're fast and it feels great, if you're bad you're slower and it doesn't have the same wow factor, which means being good is very rewarding. And the best part is there are TONS of mods for the 3D levels from all your favorite 3D games and some originals too.
Now, I mentioned mods before right? You may be wondering how can mods improve your Sonic experience. Well you clearly never played this game! I have more mod files installed than the original game content itself! There are lots of mods from stages (new and old, 2D and 3D) to music to character skins and even graphics upgrades. Don't like Sonic? There are mods for that! Don't like City Escape? Yup, you can mod it! Don't enjoy the beautiful graphics? Mod it! Needing more levels? MOD. IT. Unfortunately there's no mod for your bad taste though.
TL;DR: Best Sonic game in years, quite possibly the best Sonic game at representing what Sonic's gameplay should be all about: feeling good about going fast. I recommend this to oldschool Sonic fans, more recent fans, non-fans, young, old, everyone really. GET IT!

It's fascinating to see how a level from the newer 3D sonic games could have looked in 2D, and vice-versa. The game plays rather fun in both modes, and when you're done with each 3D/2D level there are a slew of challenges unlocked for each stage. The game knows that a big driving force in the franchise is its awesome soundtrack and uses it to its advantage. It's a pretty definitive collection for what music the series has to offer! For once, Sonic's controls are spot-on. We haven't seen this in a long, long time.
This installment is not without its glitches, despite its uncharacteristic polish. The bonus level for Rouge is badly glitched, the scoreboard is completely down, and some levels deal with game-crashing glitches. Not only is it the scene to be pointed to for how the story is horribly told through monologuing, but this boss single-handedly showcases the curse of Sonic The Hedgehog: The crash and burn that occurs when new, relatively untested elements are brought to the table. The final level is an absolute mess of poor conveyance, disorienting depth issues and various characters constantly distracting you with irrelevant tips.
This one goes on sale about five times a year for up to 75% off. However, Sonic steam keys get bundled often outside of Steam. You may want to try sites like Bundlestars and Indiegala, as they have sales with more frequency.
It's not the beacon to the promised land people are making it out to be, but Sonic Generations is cool and has a fair amount of content to keep you entertained. It's the kind of game you want to get really good at, because success within it is satisfying as hell! The Sonic formula is composed of some very fickle elements, so the impression this one leaves of true balance is rather amazing.
It's alright I guess. It's not bad by any means, it's just not really engaging even for a huge Sonic fan like me.

Now here's the gameplay
Classic Sonic (2.5D)
It feels like a HD version of the games on the genesis. The physics are not perfect, but they are close enough. Classic Sonic's stages are all 2.5D and have platforming and speed.
Modern Sonic (3D and 2.5D)
Loved the daytime stages in Sonic Unleashed? Then you will love modern sonic stages. It's like having Sonic Unleashed daytime stages on PC. The jump physics are way better in Generations than Unleashed. Also, you don't have to worry about lag! (If you have a strong enough device) I personally like playing as Modern Sonic but Classic Sonic's still fine.

Sonic's having a birthday party then the time eater comes and crashes the party. Sonic's friends all got kidnapped screaming for help. Modern Sonic meets with Classic Sonic and goes to levels to save Sonic's friends. Than, it's a final battle with Sonics vs Eggmans (Robotniks) with the help of the Time Eaters.
The Sonics turn super and defeat them and they continued the party. Classic Sonic goes back to the old time and time is now restored.
The game is overall a really great game so if you are a Sonic fan or Like sonic, I reccomend you get it.

FTL is like a fair-weather boyfriend. He's really nice, complex, and loves to have fun with you- until you do something he doesn't like or things go bad. When things go bad, he gets angry and violent and you just want to hit him.

The RNG is this game is positively ludocris and the designers had seemingly no idea what the hell an "easy" difficulty meant. I have played through this game hundreds of times and not finished it once, with more that 50% of those tries being on easy mode.
That isn't to say the game doesn't have fun moments, it's just to say that the fun you have with the game is always completely overshadowed with the overwhelming feeling of unfairness that comes with the not-so-fun moments. The Flagship is the most obvious example of this, being a boss that ostensibly has to be killed three times and gets MUCH harder everytime PIECES ARE BLOWN OFF OF IT. I love you FTL, but I have to quit you.

This is my first Ys game and I have to say that it was a really enjoyable experience. I was first introduced to Falcom games through their incredible Legend of Heroes games and I have always been curious of the Ys franchise for the past couple of years. I figured it was time to stop pondering and take the plunge into Ys Seven, their first 3d Ys title.
All in all, this game screams Falcom storytelling and action, which is a fantastic thing to behold. It took some time to get used to how the game works since I have been so used to the turn based combat of the Trails series, but once I got the hang of it, it became really fun to play.
Pros:
Excellent, fast paced combat.
Good story that draws you in over time.
Fun characters with interesting and funny dialogue.
Plenty of combat Skills that offer variaty of ways to fight.
Good soundtrack, but not even close to the quality of the Kiseki series of soundtracks.
Cons:
A lot of grinding to get everything.
Some environments were annoying to traverse, until you get the item that stops the issue.
In general, this game does many things right and I am eagerly waiting for Ys 8: Lacrimosa of Dana to make its debut onto PC soon, despite XSEED Games not being the ones helming the game. After playing Ys 7, I may consider going back to play the past Ys titles. I definitely recommend Ys 7 to be experienced by those who are: fans of the Falcom games, enjoy fast paced combat, or enjoy a good story, despite the grinding that is most definitely going to occur from the start.
Hope you all enjoy this game as much as I have!

Where to begin where to begin....
Gameplay:
Its your usual Ys action only updated in pretty much every aspect. The controls are tight , the boss fights are amazing (seriously falcom knows how to make boss fights ) , the characters and customizing them is great.
Its really easy to learn and get into AND if you know what you are doing you can with the abilities and accessories that you can get , do some really amazing combos and or just break the game in half (in a good way).
The music:
Its falcom.
The story:
Just like the other Ys games this one follows a simple formula that somehow never gets old for me. I think its mainly because the characters are so lovable in these games. Now its no trails in the sky (another falcom product) but considering Ys is more about fast gameplay that is to be expected. In the end it still managed to get a tear out of me along with other emotions.
The extra optional stuff:
Now this part is a bit tricky. You see in terms of in main game stuff , we have A LOT of stuff to do here. Optional weapons , bosses , abilities etc etc.
BUT it doesnt have the cool boss rush mode , arena modes and the upgraded versions of characters that you can unlock (then again this game has like 7 characters already soooo that is not really an issue).
The negatives:
Now before we begin these are the problems that I have encountered and it is not to say that you will too.
1: Text box glitch. It happened a lot in my run , the text boxes would flicker and while doing that you can continue (unless you press confirm at the right frame since it flickers). I actually had to reset because of this once and redo a boss fight (luckly the boss was really fun)

I imagine you play a lot of games. Probably too many but I'm not here to judge.
Maybe you play the same ones over and over again, maybe you switch from game to game looking for that one game with slick gameplay, or that game that says once and for all that games can tell amazing stories, or a game that you just want to be able to play for hours on end to let your brain sink.
And looking for the game with the great story, I imagine you've been digging pretty hard.
Which has probably led you to here.
So allow me to talk you into playing LISA.
I've played a lot of games over the years. I've played through both The Walking Dead and Undertale.
No game has brought me closer to tears than this game.
This game doesn't want to make you feel sugary, this game doesn't want to tell you everything's alright, this game doesn't want to make you feel bittersweet.
LISA is a game that wants to show you ugliness in all its forms.
And damn does it do it good.
I love the characters. The main cast is all fully fleshed out and interesting, nobody (save one) is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ "just because" or does the right thing "just because". The motivations are clear. You know these people. That's why it hurts so much to see them slowly lowered into a pool of their own ♥♥♥♥♥♥ choices. Save one, most of the party members are pretty one-sided, but they're still very interesting and fun. And there's a few with enough backstory for you to really feel for them, even though in-game they're never given their due.
I love the choices. You're not going to get a good ending. There is no "good" or "bad" ending. There's just "The End." And that's not why the choices are good. The choices you make directly affect gameplay. You could lose something you held dear, your damage dealer, your best friend, or your ♥♥♥♥ING ARM.
I love the atmosphere. I'm a sucker for the post-apocalypse but this one is particularly nice. The backgrounds, the towns, the dialouge all seems very real. This is an apocalypse formed by sloth and despair. No bombs twisted the metal, no zombies are responsible for those corpses. This happened because there's nothing left. Humanity has given up. The music is fantastic, I can think of individual overworld tracks and just about every fight track that I adore and even bought the soundtrack for. Ones that stand out are Summer Love (because of course), Muddy Waters, and Blood for Sex.
And all in all, I love the story. Everyone talks about how brutal it is, and brutal it is, but even though you go in knowing that bad♥♥♥♥♥♥happens it still hits you like a truck. I felt fear and sorrow that I thought I was incapable of playing this game. It talks about Abuse, Addiction, PTSD, and Parenthood, and none of them ever feel forced or akward. It handles mature subjects with ease.
This game does almost everything I can think of right.
This whole game was made in RPG maker. Every distinct sprite was created by one man. The soundtrack is not only 72 Tracks long, not only made by one man, but also was made IN THE TRIAL VERSION OF FRUITYLOOPS.
This game was made by someone who dearly wanted to make a game, who knew what he wanted, and was willing to work his absolute♥♥♥♥♥off to deliver the most real experience possible.
Lisa is a wet wad of hatred created from pure love. It's beautiful in a way that something so hopeful yet crushing can be.
LISA is my favorite game of all time as of this review. I desperatley encourage you to make it your own.
Edit:
When/if you play this game you are going to get fatigued during the starting area. Please, PLEASE press on after a short break because while the game is a bit open ended at the start it does really get better once it gets rolling. If you get to the area 2 crossroads and you're still not feeling it then you should consider dropping it because while I love it to death LISA isn't for everyone. It's similar to Borderlands 2 where the clunky and grindy beginning hides the much better game behind it.

Freedom Planet is a great game that combines classic Sonic The Hedgehog game play with modern voice acting and story line, while also allowing the option for classic game play without any of the story or voicing. The diverse abilities of Lilac, Carol and Milla are as different from each other as night and day..... and evening.... cuz, three characters.... three times of day..... Yeah.... The admittedly simple controls, and quick-play action with the low quality almost classic Genesis type graphics allows for nice easy play style with little to no lag on any computer. The levels are each designed to bring about some type of challenge, whether it be the stage length and just sticking until the end, a small puzzle to move on, an immense amount of enemies swarming your hide with every step, or a boss who's weakspot is so tough to find that it has you pulling your hair out to find it. In the end, this is a must play game if you like classic Sonic The Hedgehog type games, sidescrollers, epic boss battles, or just want something to play on your free time.

First off, let me say that I've always considered the classic 2D Sonic games as okay and meh. I liked the concept of a platformer focussed around active movement and light combat, but the little things like the annoying life/ring system just killed it for me. Thankfully, Freedom Planet takes the concept of Sonic the Hedgehog and greatly improves upon it with slight adjustments and new ideas that make it a true spiritual succesor worth experiencing.
Gameplay: Basically what you would expect the gameplay is mostly composed of free-running, jumping and getting your hands dirty in a scrappy fight now and then. It's all easy to learn but somewhat difficult to master what with the different factors to keep in mind like the character's magic/stamina bar, the weaknesses of the enemies as well of the current surroundings. The main character: Lilac's style is best described as graceful and practical with attacks and moves that can compliment each other once you've practiced on the first level or two, and Carol is much more adept at fighting than she is running, making her motorcycle power-up all the more entertaining and special once you get one. With their own slight strengths and weaknesses, Freedom Planet is one of the few platformer games with multiple characters in which the characters are noticeably different without one being easier to use. The only complaint I have with the overall gameplay is that you don't really get informed of the character's lesser known abilities. It was longer than I'm proud to admit before I found out that Carol can wall-jump or that Lilac can do her "cyclone" while running on the ground. But even this set-back is nothing considering that learning by doing and experimenting is always greatly preferred to the alternative of annoying tutorials and the like.
Story: Without wanting to spoil too much, the story starts out small with a hectic "political conundrum" and later builds up to a world-threatening catastrophe. Each character has their own personality with fair imperfections that become more noticeable as time goes on. I was surprised at how much subtle emotion was depicted from even the secondary characters who hardly had any screen time. It makes for an interesting set-up and gives just enough context to motivate you to keep moving forward in case the option to just skip the story isn't preferred. The worst things to say about the story is that if you decide to skip even one cutscene then you'll probably feel a bit lost when you get to the next one since a lot tends to happen in such little time, and also that the main characters in the story are so friendly and innocent that it's more than understandable why an older player might get turned away.
Anything else: All in all, this is an amazing platformer and an incredible game. It's overflowing with pure entertainment, and I find myself coming back to it more than I ever would've ever guessed when I first made my purchase. I think if anything, my favorite thing about this game is that it has more replay value than 90% of other newly released games. There isn't any doubt in my mind that I'll still be revisiting these wonderful levels five years from now.

I don't often write reviews, but I also don't often get sucked into a game as hard as I did with this one. I've always been a huge fan of the Sonic games, and while it would be accurate to say that this is inspired in some ways by classic Sonic (Sonic CD, to be more specific), it is SO much more than that, and it is a disservice to this game to say that it is a Sonic clone or knock-off.
First and foremost, this is an amazing platformer with an enormous, beautifully realized world. The sprite work is the best and most detailed of any game I've seen, and there is a ridiculous amount of enemy variety. The physics of the game are pretty good, though I'm not a fan of the super-generous wall walking. You don't really need any speed at all to climb any slope, including going upside down.
The game is also hard as nails in spots, and while it doesn't always feel fair, you will never have to redo a full stage because a boss used up all your lives. Hell, even the final boss fight is generous enough that if you get a game over during the fight you start over at the beginning of the phase you were just on.
The voice acting is a bit spotty, which should come as no surprise, since this is the first role of most of the cast. The writing can be a bit campy, but it's never so bad that it becomes unbearable.
Also, there's a ton of replay value. Time Trial mode, classic mode (no cutscenes, just action), hundreds of collectible pieces of art and music, and three playable characters all with drastically different play styles.
If you're only interested in the classic mode, or plan to skip through the cutscenes, it can be a little short... might want to wait for a sale. If you're looking for a fun game with a cute story that isn't afraid of getting dark, then you can't go wrong with Freedom Planet.

I can't believe I played this game for eight hours. Newcomers, seek a newer, better made Star Wars Jedi game. Nostalgia seekers, nothing here is going to convince you not to buy a Star Wars game.
The first two missions are shooter only, then you get a lightsaber. Here now, this is where I was hoping things would heat up, include more cool Jedi fighting. Instead, you're given a level where you have to balance shooting from a distance with up-close lightsaber action. This seems like a great game design choice at first, but the gradual difficulty climb also highlights the game's glaring mechanical errors.
For example, the sniper-section of the forementioned level is frustrating because of the clumsiness with which the sniper zooms. While standing, you can zoom, but not move. By the grace of what seems to be an overlooked game mechanic, you can crouch and keep your zoom to take out all of Greedo's brothers.
Then the lightsaber is plain disappointing. Swings pass through enemies sometimes without doing any damage, but sometimes when you turn into them without swinging, the lightsaber slices off an arm. The floppy and sloppy lightsaber mechanics drains the fun out of the best part of being a jedi.
Add onto that convoluted level design and contrived puzzles, that are difficult because the game is poorly made, and I find myself wondering why I spent so long playing this game when I have better Star Wars Jedi games waiting in my catalogue.

tl;dr Fantastic concept with a good execution... But has some strange quirks that need to be addressed.
As someone who really enjoys a tycoon game AND a glass of wine, this was right up my alley. And let me say right off the bat, I enjoy playing this game... It's interesting, follows some good tycoon concepts, and is something that you can just jump on and play for a bit. You feel accomplished when you've had awful weather throughout the growth period, and you still manage to get a 5 star rating.
However, there are some quirks that might throw new and veteran tycoon players alike.
-Money seems to be doing it's own thing. I had 3 plots of land and $50,000 in the bank, went bankrupt. Had a near-identical situation with only $15,000 and I got through just fine.
-Difficulty seems inconsistent. At the start of the game, you're thrown into the deep end, working out how to make wine. But once you've figured it out, you can easily make 5 star wines from Day 1... Then pests start to infect your crop, but you're no where near researching the technique to combat it, so you suddenly go bankrupt.
-Reward system isn't very rewarding. I've stopped opening up the chest after getting a 5 star review, it seems to do more harm than good. Having to give away 3000 bottles for free to the Army in year 2 doesn't sound all that fun... Neither does 3 months of solid rain.
-No auto-save. This is a minor gripe, but having one of the above happen and realising you haven't saved in an hour is a pretty big blow. This wouldn't be too bad if you had a bit of warning about imminent doom, but the game can sneakily drop you to -$10,000 and boom. You're at the game over screen.
All in all, I would say this is a game to check out despite the issues. The devs look to be quite active in adding new features, listening to feedback and fixing up bugs when they show up.

There's satisfaction in making good wine but for me it's not enough to endure the boring or frustrating parts although I could see why others might like it. Non-recommendation unless you like things very slow paced or are really into wine.

TL;DR: Every long-life gamer has that particular game considered life-changing. To me, Final Fantasy IX is that game. And to me, this is the best game that a life being have ever crafted. Yes, I say “life being”, not “human”, because I’m assuming aliens have their own videogames. But they won’t be as good as Final Fantasy IX.
---------------
Okay, here comes a very long review. I’ve been waiting this for so long.
First of all, completely ignore my time count on Steam for this game. I’ve put 1000h+ into it, and I can easily make a perfect run by memory. Do you know that particular favorite movie you watch every single year? Well, I do that but with this game.
I have SO many things to comment about this game. And I need to spread them.
For those who are new into the franchise, Final Fantasy IX was a big contrast compared to the close older and newer games. Yes, they kept the turn-based battles. Yes, most of the same people worked for it. Yes, it’s considered to be part of the golden era of Square Enix. But let’s look closer to see the main differences:
Firsly, and probably the first thing to notice, is that characters are more cartoon-based. They’re not that sort of adults anymore and some of them even have a very funny, friendly looking.
The world’s aesthetics also changed a lot. Final Fantasy titles are famous for combining magic and fantasy features with metallic, cyberpunk machines. FFIX crushed that second part and  they put an antique, more steampunk-like background instead of the actual machines.
The last big noticeable feature is that the class and battle system went back to the deep basics, where characters have their unique role and can only fight strictly to that [for instance, on FFVII every character could cast anything if the skill (a.k.a Materia) was properly equipped].
And now that I’ve just summarized the most basic info about FFIX… Welcome… TO THE MOST UNDERRATED TITLE OF THE WHOLE FRANCHISE!
That’s right. This game has been so irrationally denied, it makes me question humanity’s future. For Christ’s sake, even Square itself seems to be OK about forgetting this game! Lately, many hidden fans have appeared out of nowhere stating that this is their favorite FF game, but I’m not OK with this. Too late. You joined too late. The damage is already done and this title will probably never be on the top for most people. So I’ll put this game as the most underrated one. Forever.
As a vivid fan of the franchise, let me tell you something: I will NEVER understand why so many people put FFVII on Top 1. I’ve beaten that game for like 10 times already, and the question keeps coming to me every time. Have you paid attention on what you’ve played? For its year, the game was very good but the amount of flaws it has (even story-related) is just infinite. When rating a classic game, it’s just a failure when someone puts 90% nostalgia & 10% trying-to-be-objective review as their analyses.
That being said, I’ll try to detail every worth-mention thing about this game and why I think it has been so underrated. Here we go.
THE STORY
I’m pretty sure many people didn’t understand it. I’m not telling any proper detail for spoiler avoiding, but the story starts being pretty simplistic and easy to follow but the more you progress through it, the more complex it gets. It gets so complex at the end most people don’t understand the final boss! I guess Japanese narrators love to make those sort of mindf*cks. With that in mind, let me tell you something: this is the only game that has managed to make me cry.
I’ve never ever seen in any other game a party of characters that evolve and mentally grow as hugely as they do in FFIX. Everything is connected, from start to finish, and during your journey you’ll clearly see how much impact their personalities have onto both circumstances and other characters. Everyone has their way to see things, their values, and their past justifying their present and future actions… and somehow they all manage to change and mature. I swear this game teaches SO MANY life values through their characters.
Along with the characters, the story flows in a world that feels extremely alive and varied. Every place is just so different from the previous one.
Finally, the story is long. Very long considering how short most games are nowadays. In case you don’t know, this game was separated into 4 CD’s on the PSX version, and in a blind run it can perfectly provide 40-60h, depending on how much you want to explore and how many secrets you want to discover.
THE MUSIC
It’s Nobuo Uematsu. And I could finish like this.
I mean, come on. It’s one of the most iconic video game composers. How do you expect to be the music? With hundreds of tracts, FFIX soundtrack is just over the top and unique, and together with its partners (VI, VII, VIII, X…) it will be one of the most remarkable soundtracks from PSX. Ever.
THE CHARACTERS
My god, where to start…
As I have stated before, this game has some of the most powerful characters in the franchise, by far. All of them feel extremely unique and relevant, and you will PERFECTLY follow their progress and grow during the story. It is just amazing to see how varied every personality is, and how much impact it can bring to the plot. You might not like one particular way of thinking, but soon enough you’ll realize it’s there to make you think; everyone is different and we all have different points of view. And they have to be relevant. And yes, they are in FFIX. Just see all Vivi’s maturation and I dare you, I double f*cking dare you; I dare you to tell me you haven’t learnt anything from it.
Also, I want to highlight some aspects as well: Those are NOT your conventional Square Enix characters. That’s right. The main character (Zidane) is not the emo, cold-blooded guy from the famous FF games. Instead, it’s one of the first main characters of the franchise that constantly share optimism to his crew; stays on their side; puts himself and his life on risk (even when he knows he can’t do everything) to save the others, even people he doesn’t know, and he doesn’t hesitate to do so.
Last but not least: the main villain is acclaimed to be one of the best of the franchise (together with Kefka). No more super-emo guys; this is the kind of cynic who’s always a step forward and who loves to make fun of the rest.
THE UNDERRATINGS
So why is this game so underrated? To be honest, I don’t fully know. I know the reasons that puts this game on top but not why it’s been that ignores for the media.
Maybe the fact that every character has their unique role in fighting was not that appealing to people? Something I don’t understand either. To me, that makes MUCH more sense rather than seeing a brute-force guy casting a summon spell. Really.
Maybe the friendly look of the characters? Is this seriously a con to you? They look amazing to me, and definitely much better than all those weeaboo-jpop-like characters Square keeps doing in the recent games.
Maybe because it has no futuristic machines? In that case you’re just a close-minded person. And you definitely can’t appreciate how magnificent some places (like
) are.
Maybe the story looked boring to you? Then there’s no doubt you didn’t understand it. It is INFINITE TIMES more robust than FFVII storyline, and definitely way more polished, and interesting. Seriously stop overhyping that game.
In the end, every time I replay this game I start it with a feeling of “meh, I’m sure I love it because of nostalgia”. But that banishes when I reach the credits. This is still the best game I’ve ever played in my entire life, and I’ve played THOUSANDS, and completed about 700 probably. So go and buy it, see what I mean, experience this masterpiece and overall enjoy every minute of it.

I was sitting with my wife, god rest her soul, sipping on sweet lemon tea. I believe it was homemade by my sweet wife, God rest her soul. Or wait... Maybe she bought it from the store in a bottle. You know, like a plastic bottle? Well hold on now, that would be ridiculous to buy a bottle of sweet lemon tea, then transfer the contents into a glass. Why not just drink it from the bottle? I guess maybe so she could put ice in the glass? But then again, making tea homemade would be just as time consuming, if not more! That sneaky ♥♥♥♥♥... Anyway, I'll save that story for later! So, I'm sitting on my porch drinking sweet lemon tea. From a glass of course, ho ho! When suddenly... A great strangeness fills my body... Something was wrong... I've lived many years, and I've never felt something like this before. Do you know what it was? Yup! It was my rocking chair! That wooden son of a gun stopped rocking! So I looked down and realized a little rock had gotten caught beneath my chair! A rock under my rocking chair! What a day! I decided it was time for bed, I had had a little bit too much excitement for one day! Hoho! I slid into my jammies, brushed my teeth, and said my prayers. As I was climbing into bed I noticed my wife, God rest her soul, brushing her hair in the bathroom. As I peered across the hall my body swelled up with emotion...
"Why can't I be married to an attractive woman?"
"Is it me?"
"My bank account?"
I'm a tall guy, I workout forty minutes a week... Is that not enough? Now my neighbor at the time, Tom Forknight, was very short. His wife, Karen Forknight-Plateburger... Yeah, one of THOSE women. Well, she was more attractive than my wife. I'd say she was a soft six, whereas my wife was a hard four. What's the deal? I thought women liked tall men? Why was Karen with him? Anyway my horse of a wife, God rest her soul, crawled into bed next to me. She decided to leave the bedside light on so she could read her book. It was one of her romance novels again... Give me a break... As if I don't already feel inadequate enough... Not only do I have to compete with Tom, now I have to deal with these fictional hunks! Ay yai yai! At this point I had already suppressed the urges of intimacy, I rolled over and tried to sleep. Her bedside light was only of minor annoyance. I was able to drift off... Then I woke up to a big flash of light. That's about it. I can tell by the way you're walking away that you don't want to leave... If you really want to hear another story I'll tell you. Once upon a hot summer night. Sometime in July... Was it July? My local grocery store sells really good eggs in July. I don't know why. Do chickens operate better in heat? Fireworks maybe? I don't know. I don't want to get off topic. Point is, the eggs that Summer were marvelous! Anyway, my wife and I, God rest her soul, went to a BBQ that night. It was held at Dale Spooner's house.
Well, his backyard... Conny Spooner doesn't want people in her home, I think she's just an uptight ♥♥♥♥♥. So at this BBQ I see none other than... That's right, Tom Forknight... Now earlier in the day wife, God rest her soul, had made potato salad for the BBQ. Personally I hate potato salad, I'm a mashed kind of fellow. Hoho! So I sat in the TV room avoiding her till the BBQ. Once we were at the party, I made sure to distance myself from my dumb potato ♥♥♥♥♥ wife. God rest her soul, I just didn't want anyone to think I would associate with someone that would bring a potato salad! Anyway, Tom and his above mediocre wife were already there. And get this, they brought a fruit salad! With whipped cream! The nerve of those Forknights! Needless to say I gave my wife, God rest her soul, a couple choice words About whipped cream! Versus potato salad! God dammit! Son of a ♥♥♥♥♥! A real tongue lashing! Geez, you're kind of smothering me. I'll talk to you later.﻿
Well hello again! Funny seeing you here! What, are ya following me or something? Hoho! Anyway... I often wonder what all happened here. What was that big flash? Why are we here? Even our night and day cycle is odd... Sometimes days last ages, and nights come rarely. And these clouds... So strange... What's happened to our Earth? Oh well. Enough of that boring stuff. I once had a real kooky day at the doctor's office! I was in the waiting room reading a teen magazine. Normally I don't indulge in adolescent publications, but I couldn't resist! I had recently heard the new artist on the radio, Ulysess Utensils! She's some young woman, maybe a boy, I don't know. Either way that child can really grasp my attention! So I'm reading this magazine because I saw Ulysess on the cover. I still wasn't able to indentify if it was a man or woman. But as I'm reading I notice something on the ceiling... I look up to see that there is some water damage. You'd think a doctor would make enough money to maintain his office... I guess he cares about his cool jetskis more than his patient's comfort... And his assumedly big house and hard-bodied wife... I wish my wife was like that... Big ol'... Melons... Just then! A droplet of water falls from the ceiling! My eyes trail it all the way down to the ground! I stared at the floor for some time, watching the carpet absorb the water. Suddenly my attention is caught by a small child. The child was glaring directly at me. I saw the devil looking right back at me beneath his eyes! I got nervous and quickly stared directly at my feet as not to aggravate the child. And that's when I noticed something... I was wearing two different kinds of socks! Golly, I'm all revved up after these thrilling exchanges! To be fair you're a bit of a bore, but beggars can't be choosers! I think I’ll stick around, I've got many a tale to tell!﻿

First off, I'll start by saying that this is the only Gothic game I've played. Ever. So I have nothing to compare it to. In light of that, this game is really fantastic. It has a good degree of realistic difficulty( i.e no hovering arrow to show you where to go, minimalistic map, ANY enemy in the game has the potential to destroy you, wide variety of magic spells that do things other than directly hurt your target, etc.), and what I like most is that it's very well optimised for PCs that can run it. Suck it Windows 8.
Now, from what I've read, the game's story isn't actually Canon, and a little force-fed to both the player and the character. Speaking of, your character is a bit of a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but hey, I would be too if I had to be the one and only guy that can help anyone with pesky problems like fetching mushrooms, collecting taxes from townsfolk, and facilitating communications between two neighboring towns.
All in all, I'd rate this a 7/10. There is alittle room for improvement, the difficulty system is something to be desired, it only really changes the amount of enemies in their groups found around the world, and little else. You can probably steam-roll through this game and finish it in about roughly 5 hours, excluding exploration and side-quests.

-Decent plot for single player

-You can replay missions any number of times
-The developer is very kind and has quickly replied to (at least my) concerns (bugs and the like), and is generally a very nice person in my experience.

Oh boy here we go. I first bought this game when I was 11 years old, in a Best Buy a few months after it was released in 2002. It was the first video game I ever bought with my own money and I remember my dad asking me if I was sure I wanted this as $50 was a lot to an 11 year old. I nodded and pointed to the force lightning picture on the back and away we went.
Over the next year I played exclusively with bots in offline multiplayer as I couldn't figure out how to see the serverlist for online play. But It wasn't a big deal as I was having fun already. One day when I tried refreshing the server list out of habit,  it finally loaded! Out pops all these servers spanning all the gametypes for thousands of players currently online. Definitely jaw-dropping. What's nice is back then the game was super social and everyone was figuring out how things worked. Just knowing how to set your name in colors back then would set you apart from many, rofl.
So I played. A lot. I messed around in cheats servers, learning how to crush people with the viewpos command. I made friends with all different kinds of people and from all over the world. I roleplayed by pretending I was older, younger, male, female, movie characters, anime characters, whatever, you name it. Movies like Lord of the Rings were just coming out and that showed in game as people then started making skins and maps like Helms Deep. It was the first time I was exposed to something I could get lost in, and I could be whoever I wanted to be.
Then came CTF. I started getting bored with FFA and being this inquisitive baby nerd I ventured out of my comfort zone in search for more. I started seeing people hopping around the maps moving insanely fast, but force is disabled here so wtf dude? how? So I sat in spectator with my little mental notepad pondering how people did these things and down the rabbit hole I went. The more I played the more I learned how much I didn't know, which lead to me wanting to learn more.
Life outside jk2 was pretty bleh. My grades went down, I lost friends, or rather I stopped hanging out as much with them outside of school. I lost interest in previous hobbies and couldn't garner up much motivation to learn new things.  My parents grounded me more and more in attempts to try and solve this issue. My emotions were all over the place.
But I didn't quit, as the game meant more to me than anything else. And no one could understand where I was coming from, except my friends online. So I did the bare minimum irl. I learned to be more deceptive to appease people as I got through my angsty phase, and I kept playing.
Then something happened I wasn't really expecting. The game's playerbase started to dwindle. In around 2010 basically nobody was playing CTF (which became my favorite gametype), minus the euro population who I didn't really get involved with much. I realized that my favorite thing was dying and it made me sad because it appeared I didn't gain much from all my hours invested. My parents, siblings, everyone thought I was insane at this point, and nobody really knew me for who I was.
I decided I would try and explore different things. I took up different video games, reading, going to raves, dancing, guitar, martial arts, etc and yeah, I had fun, but I felt disconnected from everyone else and couldn't really get into anything to the same degree as I did with jk2.  Life just kinda meandered along. Sometimes jk2 games would get going and I would play to satisfy my cravings. But ugh, playing again lead me to get addicted again and again despite how much I've played and how little people were left.
My first semester of college was pretty rough and I think I ended with a .7 for my GPA, This landed me on academic probabation and in major trouble with my family. I couldn't bring myself to go to classes and I hated everyone and everything. At this rock bottom point in my life, stuff had to change otherwise this wasn't going to end well. It was eye-opening to me because I felt like how I did early on in jk2, like I could do anything I wanted, just be happy, jeez. So I got the confidence to conquer my bucket list and things I repressed out of fear. I started taking hormones, I travelled around the world, I switched my major, I dated more, I learned how to cook, ride motorcycles, and I found a new passion, poker, HAH. All big stuff for me, and I'm a lot happier now. My boyfriend and I have plans to marry, and we're both getting our careers going. But through all the good and the bad times I had growing up, JK2 was always there for me, and it's the only reason I mention all this sappy stuff in a ♥♥♥♥ing game review.
~30,000 hours of jk2 later, I'm now about to turn 25 :) I got pretty good at this game, never was the best, but got to a level I was happy with.The only game I really play now is poker, and I'm using this whole star wars experience as a motivator to show me what I can accomplish with a lot of dedication. This game really taught me about how important time management is, having a balanced lifestyle, and having an open and inquisitive mind. My thanks to the developers for making it, and to everyone who I met and played with. Lastly, to those who played such crazy amounts as me, I hope you found happiness in other places and can look back on this game with a smile.
Cali.

Let's start off with the difficulty. If you prefer games to hold your hand and show you exactly where to go, then you will not enjoy Jedi Outcast. No matter what difficulty you're on, the puzzles can be quite mind-boggling. I've beaten the majority of the 3D Zelda games, and I had a much harder time with the puzzles in this game. I highly recommend the Medium (Jedi) or Low (Padawan) difficulties for your first playthrough. I chose Hard (Jedi Knight) I got my a$$ handed to me for quite awhile until I began to understand the mechanics. I should mention that the first quarter or so of the game you're forced to only use guns, and it's really just not fun. I absolutely love FPS games, but something about this just feels wrong. Luckily, you can install a mod that will let you start out with your force powers and lightsaber. Yes, this is story-breaking, but it's worth it for the enjoyment of the gameplay.

What I thought of "YS Seven"
I can't fully compare this to all other Ys Games. It's by far the most different Ys game compaired to all the rest even 1 & 2. That said before playing this game I loved the Ys Series but I did not consider it to be one of the greats! Like The Tales of series or Final Fantasy etc. Ys Seven changes that. Is it at least in my opinion the best overall Ys Game. Sure other Ys games are better in some aspects but this is the first Ys game that feels massive. And yes playing the previous Ys game only adds to the greatness of Ys Seven.
Let me exsplain. This is the first Ys game to have a whole party of charachters and you can have three in your active party at once. The A.I allys are good enough to not get in the way. And this game refuses to end. I was maybe 50%-60% into the game and I thought I was at the very end. It took almost seven hours after that point just to reach the final duneon. So while most Ys games will go for about 5-15 hours game play. Ys Seven is more like 25+ hours and I have yet to finish all side goals to 100% so I may play a little longer.

The combat and attack controls are pretty good no complaints here. Since the game is longer and has many areas the enemies feel a little re-used but only compaired to other Ys Games. But still they get the job done and feel original enough that it's fine.  The boss fights are intense and even though you can use a lot of healing items even during boss battles which is uncommon in Ys it's very difficult. Your going to need to grind exp and loot to win.  Level design is very good. Actually level design is close to the best I have seen Ys offer. No major issues I have with the game. This is my favorite Ys game but the story and chrarachters are way better than other Ys games. I still feel the combat itself is still better represented in Ys Orgin but overall Ys Seven rocks!

Reviewing Ys? Should be automatic at this point! :)
Ys is one of those series which really never fail at every title (Ys I and II to me are awesome games too).
Ys 7 translates all to a 3D plain, and I can't help but think often at Final Fantasy VII for many things. Graphics are great, and as always the soundtrack is really amazing.
For what concerns the gameplay - fully supported XBOX controller, no cheap USB controller though, the one I used with Ys Origins and the other older games - everything runs so smoothly and fast that I can only love it. An action RPG is not a turn-based/strategy game and to me it needs to be fast, transitions need to be fast, and here really I have never experienced a single problem.
You're provided with lots of options, equipment, magic, skills, everything. And it's all scaled so that you start at level 1 and get accustomed to the world, to the new kinds of skills etc. with playing time; there's nothing out of place. You have also the standard Ys difficulty options from easy onwards (four levels unlocked from the start), just in case you're a beginner - however, being this a 3D game advanced in the series, I'd suggest to start with some previous titles available here on Steam too.
All the characters have their own weapons and strength towards enemies, and you can switch between them with just one key; boss fights are more challenging than ever (ok, Ys Origin at times was very difficult XD) and here the game shines even more than during the usual fights that are scatteret through the maps.
Since I'm not a console player I really don't want to say nothing about PSP ports and such; I just talk about this game on Steam, and it runs perfectly! And apart from this everyone says it's even better here than in its original vest, so.. ahah :)
The screen fits all - a perfect minimap, HP, SP, EXP and everything on lower right, enemy stats on the left and so on; really, I rarely saw a game so perfect in every detail and I think that a PC and not a portable console is the best way to enjoy Ys 7. It also features all my favourite things, like, a button to optimize equipment, shortcuts, skipping dialogues.. everything! :)
The plot isn't that thorough, but still definitely enjoyable with also hints to previous titles. You have also lots of sidequest and such; just the achievements to me aren't that greatly placed 'cos they're almost all like "get all the skills", "get everyone to the maximum level".. I think that in RPGs achievements must follow the player from his first steps to the last boss, but anyways, this doesn't affect gameplay.
It's definitely a must to have even if the Ys series isn't super known at least here in Europe; there aren't so many action RPGs better than these and the Seven release really stands up at its best.

Though I’m a long time series fan of Ys, I’ve never played the more recent games designed for PSP and Vita. I just don’t play games portably. So it’s with fresh eyes I played this PC port of Ys Seven. It’s probably the worst Ys game Falcom has made in the 2000s. By regular RPG standards, this is above average. But it doesn’t live up to the standards I’ve come to expect from Ys. And it certainly isn’t a worthy follow-up to Ys Origin.
What makes the Ys series unique is its energetic music, and how it uses deceptively simple mechanics to maximum effect. I don't know of anything that quite captures the same sense of speed and control the way Ys does. Because of the camera perspective, the series has been able to throw an almost bullet hell level of chaos on screen without it feeling unfair. Third person games like Bayonetta or Metal Gear Rising might have a sense of speed and spectacle, but their camera puts limits on how chaotic they can be before you lose control of what's happening. Ys never had that problem.
The traditional weakness of Ys has been the story, as it’s often bare bones and archetypal. But the series has been around since the 1980s, so it’s been largely on par with the genre as a whole over time. With Ys Origin, the developers aimed higher than usual, and delivered a truly great story for the first time. Unfortunately, in Ys Seven, they stumbled backward into the more archetypal, bland, and unexciting type of stories they were doing before. But in this case with the unpleasant addition of too much text. There are loads of characters in this story, and there's no point to half of them. Ys Origin was nothing like this. It had a vivid cast, with clear motivations, and a focus on what mattered. It made me care. For the majority of Ys Seven, I was bored by the story. Now and then it provided a blip of excitement, but it wasn't enough to make up for the bad parts.
As for how it plays, this feels like an Ys game operating at 75% intensity. For the first time in the series you control a whole party of characters, and this results in visual chaos. You don't get the same level of precision from this new combat system. And I guess to compensate for this new system being more chaotic, you're given more healing items than ever before. As the first game using this system, it isn't bad, but the unique qualities that made Ys good have been diluted and makes the game more ordinary. It has its moments, like the boss fights. Now and then everything clicked, and I got a huge smile on my face. It just didn't happen as regularly as I expect from Ys. For the most part combat in this feels more laid back, not as demanding of the player. It's too bad because it feels like it lost some of the purpose for why you'd even play a Ys game to begin with.
Ys Seven is disappointing in another critical aspect, and that's the music. There are loads of different tracks in the game, but almost none of them are notable. Falcom has a heritage of making the best game music in history, and delivering a soundtrack that's merely adequate is not good enough. Like with the story and combat, there are a couple times the music does its job well, but 90% of the time, it's just kind of there, not being memorable in the least. If this was a different franchise, the music would be more than good enough. But if you make a game with a history, you have things you need to live up to.
Adding on to my pile of complaints, this is an ugly game. It’s all because it came out on PSP. Ys Seven looks better than an N64 game, but not by much. On the original PSP screen, I’m sure this looked adequate. But I played this on a 65” TV in 4K, and the technical compromises were too obvious. It's unfortunate, because all the other Ys games made in the 2000s with PC as the primary platform, like Ys 6, have a timeless quality to them. Their use of 3D and 2D scales beautifully to any screen size. The problem is, that it’s an aesthetic not even the PS2 was able to handle. When Ys 6 was ported to PS2, they had to make the game look worse for it to run properly. And when it came to making Ys Seven I’m sure they did their best with what they had to work with, but I kinda wish they’d made this a 2D game instead. The PSP was simply too crappy to do this game justice.
For Ys series fans, I’d still recommend Ys Seven. Just temper your expectations a bit. Even though this is the worst Ys game I've played since Ys 5, it's still better than your average RPG. Combat still requires you learn enemy patterns and time dodges, as you can't brute force your way to victory by grinding levels or items. And it's relatively free from tedium. Probably the absolute worst sequence in the game is how it opens, as it took me 40 minutes of running around town before the game let me explore the first field and fight monsters. After that, it stuck closely to the template established by Ys 6. Even if I'm disappointed with how this game turned out, there's still enough of what I want from Ys in here that I went away reasonably happy. I just wanted a more potent and powerful Ys experience. Guess I'll have to put my hopes in the next game, whenever it comes out on PC.

A truthful depiction of the struggles of making it in the wine industry. Fun and worth the price, although it could use some work. Not a perfect viticulture and oenology simulator, and could use some more depth, but I enjoy it.
A few nitpicky points:
I think it's far too easy to lose the game, a few bad vintages in a row and you're likely bankrupt.
Oak as the first tier fermenter rather than Steel is a bit wierd considering how expensive it is these days.
Limited Varietals and Limited use of them. With only Cab. Sauv, Sauv. Blanc, Syrah/Shiraz, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Merlot, the game feels a bit much like an exercise in International Varieties, No Pinot Grigio/Gris, no Cab Franc, No Muscat, No Semillon, no Petit Verdot, no Chenin Blanc, no Gewurztraminer, no Riesling, no Verdelho.
No Blends. It's an important part of the wine industry, come on, GSM, Meritage, Bordeaux?
There's no ability to mitigate faults, like using overripe grapes to make dessert wine, Vin Jaune, or Brandy
I'd like to see a system for Sherry but I feel like that's a bit much in terms of depth.
I'd like to see a system where you can sell grapes to another producer or buy someone else's grapes for your own, but that might be going a bit too far.
The Grape tiering and soil tiering doesn't really make a great deal of sense in my opinion, the Terroir doesn't really change any characteristic of the grape because all varietals are locked to a specific soil type. Some of my favourite Shiraz is grown in Clay.

This game fits in a weird niche, being both hard, somehow frantic, and yet slow and relaxing. Others have already described the mechanics of the game, so I won't indulge in another long review of them: this game is just intriguing. It nails perfectly the feel of having to deal with a real vineyard, the difficulty of mantaining a little business and the delicate balance needed to make a great wine. It's a difficult balance that for some may sound too hard or slow (you don't really start to improve your Chateau before years and years of GOOD wine..And a couple of bad years may destroy everything you've built), but if you want a good simulation game and don't care about a slow growth, this game is for you.

The tycoon game genre has been one of my favorite genres since I was a kid.  I’ve played Zoo Tycoon, Lemonade Tycoon, Mall Tycoon (which was terrible), and of course the amazing Roller Coaster Tycoon which I have played into adulthood and continue to enjoy to this day. These games are simple on the surface, but once you immerse yourself into the mechanics, you open up a whole new world of money making possibilities that make the replay value endless.
Terroir is wine making tycoon game that has the player planting grapes of different varieties, ripening them to the correct number, and then trying to turn the resulting harvest into the perfect wine through the four winemaking processes: crushing, fermentation, pressing, and ageing.  Certain grapes can only be planted in specific ground types.  Tiles like forests and lakes provide bonus modifiers such as protection from certain afflictions with the lake and an increased output for your vines next to a forest tile.
Terroir really tries to fit into this genre by being complex and unique like the product featured in the game, but unfortunately, it becomes simple and unfair when you boil it down.  There is way too much randomness to the game to implement any strategy that can further the game in a meaningful way.  You could have had a great previous couple of years and finally be able to afford to buy a new tile and plant new grapes, but if the following year is bad, you risk losing the game completely.
This game is frustratingly unforgiving with mistakes as well.  Several times during my time with the game, I would accidentally buy a tile I didn’t want or realized I couldn’t afford the type of grapes on the soil type.  There is no refund system or sell land option so I had no choice but to restart the game.  The already slow pace of the game is made even worse due to how expensive everything is.  Growing grapes quickly drains your account, bottling costs thousands, and simple things such as pesticide research kept eluding my grasp due to bad years.
Bad years seem to happen more often than not; many times I have lost a game due to way too much rain or none at all.  You can lose your entire crop if you miss harvesting by December.  They don’t gradually deplete either, they immediately vanish all at once, and this simple mistake can cost you the game.  I get that they are trying to make this game realistic with the random weather and limited time to harvest, but the treasure chest system removes any realism they may have wanted in the game.  When you craft a wine that receives five stars, you are able to open a chest which allows you to choose between chance and circumstance.  This would be fine if this acted like a reward, but these often wound up being to my detriment and sometimes even caused me to lose.  Occasionally this chest would give me a little bonus money, but it usually made me lose money, experience bad weather, or even get extorted by the army.
Even on easy mode, you are at the mercy of the game’s RNG system which would be fine if the game wasn’t so punishing in every other aspect.  Also, once you figure out how to create the perfect five star wine stat combinations, experimentation ends, and I just found myself stressing about weather conditions and doing math to make sure it would come out just right.  There is never a time where I felt accomplished or could relax because I always knew that even if I was doing well, if I upgrade just a little too much and have a bad year, the game is over.
Before I conclude this review, let’s cover the graphics and music.  I don’t mind the simplistic graphics of Terroir, but I wish they had added a little more detail with the sky or changed the UI to make the game visually interesting while I’m staring at the weather, month, and ripeness numbers.  The sound effects are serviceable, but the music gets repetitive fairly quickly and I switched to my own. (Note: after playing the game for a bit after my review, the music grew on me more)
Terroir feels like a game that should still be in early access even though they recently announced that it is fully released.  I’m hoping they listen to the reviews on Steam and improve/remove the different aspects that really need it.  Having a loot chest style reward felt very out of place in this game, and I never got into a groove with the game or felt successful which is very important with a tycoon style game.
I give Terroir 2.5 stars out of 5.  I see the potential of a very fun tycoon game, but they need to allow the player to speed up the time even more or increase the pace in some other way.  It takes too long to get going, and even when it does, you can fail due to RNG.

Freedom Planet is a Sonic the Hedgehog-inspired 2D platformer, but it’s far from being a shallow rip-off. It’s one of those games that takes obvious inspiration out of classics from the 16-bit era, but it does it in a way that it feels fresh and has its own identity. The game gives you the option to play as three characters: Sash Lilac, Carol Tea and Milla Basset. The game’s story is fairly simple, but it has some interesting twists somewhere down the line. It’s definitely an enjoyable one and keeps you engaged with the game.
The gameplay is outstanding. While boss battles and certain moves can be quite tricky on the first try, it definitely feels rewarding to master the mechanics of the game and defeat your adversaries. At first, it feels very Sonic-y in terms of gameplay, but it also has some MegaMan and Beat’em Up elements if you ask me.
Freedom Planet definitely excels in the sound department. I can just listen to the soundtrack for hours; its tracks appropriately fit the stages and scenarios they’re designed for. The voice acting is pretty good as well, most notably towards Lilac, Torque and Brevon. I can’t really point out some major flaws besides the occasional difficulty curve and the desire to want more out of this game (story, stages, characters).
With 4 to 6 hours per character gameplay and dozens of achievements that demand quite some skill and mastery, Freedom Planet is a homage to 16-bit furry sidescrollers that feels fresh and plays tremendously enjoyable till the very end.

Freedom Planet - the moment I stepped into this game, I thought that it looked like a Sonic game, and according to the thousand-something other reviewers, I'm not alone. Avoiding the temptation of calling it a Sonic analog, what is Freedom Planet?
Freedom Planet is a 2d platformer with emphasis on speed and combat. Every girl is capable of going blindingly fast, so much that it can be hard to keep up with them; they can use this speed to climb up walls, outrun enemies, and soar up to otherwise hard-to-reach areas. There's no RPG element - the characters have all the powers needed to clear the game from the moment you pick them.
The protagonists each have their own little quirks that come out in the game's many cutscenes. Those that do not like the voice acting will be pleased to know that every cutscene can be skipped - those who do like cutscenes will find a pleasantly colorful story. Opinions will vary as to whether or not the writing is good, though it is the likeable characters which help pull everything together. For a game that is trying to keep its rating child-friendly, the villain is also surprisingly brutal; where some villains are content to yell "I'll get you next time!" as the hero thwarts them, Lord Brevon acts as more of the "I don't think you really -need- to breathe right now" sort of antagonist.
One of the best aspects of the game would have to be the astoundingly well done sound track. Moody tracks play during tense combat-heavy levels, whereas up-beat or thrilling songs play during faster levels. Many of these tracks are great to listen to even outside the game, ranging between atmospheric and electronica for a nice diverse blend of background music. With 3 hours with of very well done music, the soundtrack is worthy of consideration.
Levels are well done and fun to go through. If one is more of an explorer, there are hidden nooks and crannies everywhere hiding little hidden power ups, crystals, and 'cards' that unlock sound files and concept art. If a person is the sort who prefers fast paced action, 'feeling' the level as they go, many of the levels challenge players to plow through them as fast as possible for the best time. Both the adrenaline junkie and the completionist will likely find a home in this game thanks to its wide yet free flowing design.
Any criticism I have on the game is mostly nitpicking. I would have liked a proper borderless fullscreen mode [Edit: ten hours in, I found it], better volume control, and more importantly the ability to access the options menu while playing.
I suppose I could also criticize the game's length, but I feel that is more of a testament to how enjoyable it is than an actual matter of content. At about 3.5 hours for a non-speed run playthrough, and of course a possible second or third playthrough with different characters, it still feels like we're only scratching the surface of what the world of Avalice has to offer. Heck, I'm itching for a sequel already, and this game has free DLC that has yet to be released.
Freedom Planet is what an indie game -should- look like. Exciting, enthralling and imaginative, this is probably one of the best recent indie games to hit the proverbial shelves. Where some games pretentiously show off one quirky mechanic the developers came up with, Freedom Planet excels in multiple areas, managing to be great almost everywhere without being faulty anywhere.
Some call it the new 'Sonic', and perhaps they're right. But maybe, just maybe, we may also be witnessing the start of something greater. A WiiU adaptation is already in the works as of this writing, and perhaps there will be more Freedom Planet in the future; we'll see.
For anyone looking for a little indie game that is not only adorable with its characters but also adrenaline-inducing in its gameplay, Freedom Planet is highly recommended.

Now for the bad though, it's technically not great (is this genre cursed?), it's a Unity engine game that's capped at 30fps, you have to edit the registry to fix this which is easy enough to do but you'll notice straight away the game is optimised for 30fps, even on medium settings I couldn't hit 60fps in all situations (although to be fair, I did most of the time). This will lead to many occasions where you'll cycle between to camera angles, which can get frustrating.
The storyline is pretty solid and surprisingly less predictable than I thought.  I was drawn in quite well by how the story unfolded.  The voice acting was pretty decent throughout the game (it's not the best of Hollywood, but it can hold its own and it's believable).
Replayability:  Admittedly, the storyline doesn't have enough variation to warrant replay.  I went back to get a few of the achievements, but it was too tedious to go through everything again.  But let's be honest: There aren't many storyline driven games that are interesting enough to draw me back in for multiple play-throughs.
All-in-all, it's a good game.  It may not be for everyone, but it is appealing to those who love story-driven games.  It was a good casual game that I could play without bending my brain too much.  But don't get the game expecting loads of action or seriously challenging puzzles...because it's not like that.
